questions.question: What is a group of web pages that groups of individuals can edit and view together called?
questions.explanation: Podcasting and blogs allow the one-way dissemination of information. Instant messaging allows the synchronous communication between individuals. A wiki allows groups of individuals to view and edit web pages collaboratively.

questions.question: Which of the following are disadvantages of peer-to-peer networking? (Choose two.)
options: Expensive to set up and maintain
questions.explanation: Peer-to-peer networks are inexpensive and easy to configure but lack any centralized management and do not scale well. The two disadvantages are: No centralized administration and Scalability.

questions.question: Which devices would be considered end devices on a network? (Choose four.)
questions.imageAlt: A network diagram with a switch, printer, IP phone, server, tablet, and wireless access point.
questions.imageCaption: Use the diagram to identify end devices.
questions.explanation: End devices form the interface between users and the underlying network. Printer, IP phone, Server, and Tablet computer are end devices. Switch and Wireless access point are intermediate/infrastructure devices.

questions.question: What type of information would be found on a logical topology diagram?
options: Length and type of all cable runs
questions.explanation: Logical topology diagrams identify devices, ports, and IP addressing schemes. Physical topology diagrams identify the physical location of intermediate devices, configured ports, and cable installations.

questions.question: What is a network infrastructure that provides access to other networks over a wide geographic area?
questions.explanation: A wide-area network (WAN) provides access to other networks over a wide geographic area. A MAN spans an area larger than a LAN. A WLAN is similar to a LAN, and a SAN is designed for data storage.

questions.question: Which of the following are business-class Internet connection technologies normally supplied by a service provider? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Leased lines and Metro Ethernet are considered business-class Internet connection technologies. Mobile services and broadband cable are technologies used to connect remote users.

questions.question: Which technology would be best to provide a home user with a high-speed, always-on Internet connection?
questions.explanation: DSL is an always-on technology that offers good bandwidth at reasonable cost. Dialup and cellular are not always-on. Satellite and cellular are also relatively expensive.

questions.question: What is a converged network?
options: A network that makes use of both fiber-optic and copper connections.
A network where voice, video, and data move over the same infrastructure.
A network that makes use of both wired and wireless technology.
A network that makes use of both satellite and terrestrial connections to move data.
questions.explanation: A converged network is where voice, video, and data move over the same infrastructure. The underlying infrastructure can be wired or wireless.

questions.question: What is a fault-tolerant network?
options: A network that can provide priority treatment of voice and video traffic
A network that offers secure transactions
A network that can reroute traffic in case of device failure
A network that is incapable of failing
questions.explanation: A fault-tolerant network can continue to function if an intermediate device or path fails. It can still fail if a sufficient number of intermediate devices and/or paths fail.

questions.question: Which type of traffic must receive the highest priority from QoS?
questions.explanation: QoS prioritizes data based on sensitivity to network delay. VoIP is very sensitive to network delay and must receive priority treatment.

questions.question: What is true of Tier 3 ISPs?
options: They act as local providers of service directly to end users.
They connect directly to Tier 1 ISPs.
They interconnect with other Tier 1 ISPs.
They provide high-speed redundant services to other ISPs.
questions.explanation: Tier 3 ISPs are the local providers of service to end users. They normally connect to Tier 2 providers for Internet access.

questions.question: What are the primary requirements of information security? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Information security requires: Confidentiality (only intended recipients access data), Integrity (data not altered in transit), and Availability (information accessible in a timely manner). QoS and Scalability are not primary requirements.

questions.question: Match each network type with its description.

pairs.right: A network in a limited local area
A network over a wide geographic area
A local network that uses wireless access
A network designed for data storage

matchOptions: A network in a limited local area
A network over a wide geographic area
A local network that uses wireless access
A network designed for data storage
A private network for employees inside an organization
A network that provides controlled access to business partners
A global public network made of interconnected networks
questions.explanation: LANs cover local areas, WANs connect wide areas, WLANs provide wireless local access, and SANs are specialized for storage traffic.

questions.question: A wide-area network is abbreviated as ____.
questions.explanation: WAN stands for wide-area network, which provides access over a wide geographic area.

questions.question: A company is contemplating whether to use a client/server or a peer-to-peer network. What are three characteristics of a peer-to-peer network? (Choose three.)
options: Better device performance when acting as both client and server
questions.explanation: Peer-to-peer networks are easy to create and have lower costs because network devices and dedicated servers are not required. They also lack centralized administration and are less secure and less scalable than client/server networks.

questions.question: Which device performs the function of determining the path that messages should take through internetworks?
questions.explanation: A router determines the path that messages should take through an internetwork. A firewall filters traffic, and a DSL modem provides Internet connectivity.

questions.question: What two criteria are used to help select a network medium from various network media? (Choose two.)
options: The types of data that need to be prioritized
The cost of the end devices utilized in the network
The distance the selected medium can successfully carry a signal
The number of intermediary devices installed in the network
The environment where the selected medium is to be installed
questions.explanation: Media selection depends on factors such as distance, installation environment, required throughput, and the cost of the medium and installation.

questions.question: Which two statements describe intermediary devices? (Choose two.)
options: Intermediary devices direct the path of the data.
Intermediary devices connect individual hosts to the network.
Intermediary devices initiate the encapsulation process.
questions.explanation: Intermediary devices connect hosts to the network and direct data through the network. End-device applications generate and alter data content and initiate encapsulation.

questions.question: What are two functions of end devices on a network? (Choose two.)
options: They originate the data that flows through the network.
They direct data over alternate paths in the event of link failures.
They filter the flow of data to enhance security.
They are the interface between humans and the communication network.
They provide the channel over which the network message travels.
questions.explanation: End devices originate network data and are the interface between users and the communication network. Intermediary devices direct and filter traffic, while media carry the signal.

questions.question: Which area of the network would a college IT staff most likely have to redesign as a direct result of many students bringing their own tablets and smartphones to school to access school resources?
questions.explanation: Student tablets and smartphones most commonly access school resources through the campus wireless LAN, so that is the area most likely to need redesign.

questions.question: An employee at a branch office is creating a quote for a customer and needs to access confidential pricing information from internal servers at the Head Office. What type of network would the employee access?
questions.explanation: An intranet is a private organizational network that is accessible only to authorized members, employees, or other approved users.

questions.question: Which two connection options provide an always-on, high-bandwidth Internet connection to computers in a home office? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Cable and DSL both provide high-bandwidth, always-on Internet connections to a host computer or home LAN.

questions.question: Which two Internet connection options do not require that physical cables be run to the building? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Cellular uses the mobile network, and satellite is often used where physical cabling is not available.

questions.question: Which term describes the state of a network when the demand on the network resources exceeds the available capacity?
questions.explanation: Congestion occurs when demand on network resources exceeds available capacity.

questions.question: Which expression accurately defines the term bandwidth?
options: A method of limiting the impact of a hardware or software failure on the network
A measure of the data carrying capacity of the media
A state where the demand on the network resources exceeds the available capacity
A set of techniques to manage the utilization of network resources
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is a measure of the data carrying capacity of the media.

questions.question: Which networking trend involves the use of personal tools and devices for accessing resources on a business or campus network?
questions.explanation: BYOD, or bring your own device, allows users to use personal devices and tools on business and campus networks.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of a converged network?
options: It provides only one path between the source and destination of a message.
It limits the impact of a failure by minimizing the number of devices affected.
It delivers data, voice, and video over the same network infrastructure.
It requires a separate network infrastructure for each type of communication technology.
questions.explanation: A converged network carries multiple services, such as data, voice, and video, over the same infrastructure.

questions.question: Which statement describes a characteristic of cloud computing?
options: A business can connect directly to the Internet without the use of an ISP.
Applications can be accessed over the Internet by individual users or businesses using any device, anywhere in the world.
Devices can connect to the Internet through existing electrical wiring.
Investment in new infrastructure is required in order to access the cloud.
questions.explanation: Cloud computing lets users access applications and resources over the Internet from many device types and locations.

questions.question: Which statement describes the use of powerline networking technology?
options: New smart electrical cabling is used to extend an existing home LAN.
A home LAN is installed without the use of physical cabling.
A device connects to an existing home LAN using an adapter and an existing electrical outlet.
Wireless access points use powerline adapters to distribute data through the home LAN.
questions.explanation: Powerline networking uses adapters and existing electrical outlets to connect devices to a home LAN.

questions.question: What security violation would cause the most amount of damage to the life of a home user?
options: Denial of service to your email server
Replication of worms and viruses in your computer
Capturing of personal data that leads to identity theft
Spyware that leads to spam emails
questions.explanation: Identity theft caused by captured personal data can be more damaging to a home user than spam, malware replication, or denial of service.

questions.question: A user is implementing security on a small office network. Which two actions would provide the minimum security requirements for this network? (Choose two.)
options: Adding a dedicated intrusion prevention device
questions.explanation: A firewall and antivirus or antimalware software are common minimum security requirements for small or home networks.

questions.question: A converged network is capable of delivering voice, video, text, and graphics over the same ____.
questions.explanation: A converged network carries different communication forms over the same communication channels.

questions.question: The acronym ____ refers to the policy that allows employees to use their personal devices in the business office to access the network and other resources.
questions.explanation: BYOD stands for bring your own device.

questions.question: What are two functions of intermediary devices on a network? (Choose two.)
options: They are the primary source and providers of information and services to end devices.
They run applications that support collaboration for business.
They form the interface between the human network and the underlying communication network.
They direct data along alternate pathways when there is a link failure.
They filter the flow of data, based on security settings.
questions.explanation: Intermediary devices can direct data along alternate paths and filter data flows based on security settings.

questions.question: Match the description to the form of network communication.

pairs.left: An audio-based medium that allows people to deliver recordings to a wide audience
Interactive websites where people create and share user-generated content with friends and family
Web pages that groups of people can edit and view together
Real-time communication between two or more people

questions.explanation: Podcast, social media, wiki, and instant messaging are different forms of network communication.

questions.question: Match each characteristic to its corresponding Internet connectivity type.

pairs.left: High bandwidth connection that runs over telephone line
Not suited for heavily wooded areas
Uses coaxial cable as a medium

questions.explanation: DSL uses telephone lines, dial-up is low bandwidth, satellite needs a clear line of sight, and cable uses coaxial cable.

questions.question: What is the Internet?
options: It is a network based on Ethernet technology.
It provides network access for mobile devices.
It provides connections through interconnected global networks.
It is a private network for an organization with LAN and WAN connections.
questions.explanation: The Internet is a global system of interconnected networks that enables many types of networked devices to communicate.

questions.question: Match the definition to the security goal.

pairs.right: Only the intended recipients can access and read the data
The assurance that the information has not been altered during transmission
The assurance of timely and reliable access to data

matchOptions: Only the intended recipients can access and read the data
The assurance that the information has not been altered during transmission
The assurance of timely and reliable access to data
The ability of a network to grow without affecting users
The ability to reroute traffic after a failure
questions.explanation: Confidentiality controls access, integrity protects data from unauthorized alteration, and availability ensures timely reliable access.

questions.question: What type of network must a home user access in order to do online shopping?
questions.explanation: Online shopping requires access to the Internet.

questions.question: What type of network traffic requires QoS?
questions.explanation: Video conferencing is sensitive to delay and jitter, so it benefits from QoS treatment.

questions.question: A network administrator is implementing a policy that requires strong, complex passwords. Which data protection goal does this policy support?
questions.explanation: Strong passwords help ensure that only authorized users can access data, supporting confidentiality.

questions.question: What are two characteristics of a scalable network? (Choose two.)
options: Grows in size without impacting existing users
Is not as reliable as a small network
Suitable for modular devices that allow for expansion
questions.explanation: A scalable network can grow with limited impact on existing users and often uses modular devices that allow expansion.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Which set of devices contains only intermediary devices?
questions.imageAlt: Network diagram with devices labeled A through J.
questions.imageCaption: Identify the set that contains only intermediary devices.
questions.explanation: The set A, B, D, G contains intermediary network devices such as switching, routing, wireless routing, and firewall devices.

questions.question: Which two statements about the relationship between LANs and WANs are true? (Choose two.)
options: Both LANs and WANs connect end devices.
WANs connect LANs at slower speed bandwidth than LANs connect their internal end devices.
WANs must be publicly-owned, but LANs can be owned by either public or private entities.
WANs are typically operated through multiple ISPs, but LANs are typically operated by single organizations or individuals.
questions.explanation: WANs commonly connect LANs over lower-speed links and are often operated through multiple service providers, while LANs are usually operated by a single organization or individual.

questions.question: Which statement describes a network that supports QoS?
options: The fewest possible devices are affected by a failure.
The network should be able to expand to keep up with user demand.
The network provides predictable levels of service to different types of traffic.
Data sent over the network is not altered in transmission.
questions.explanation: QoS provides predictable service levels to different traffic types by managing network resource use.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of circuit-switched networks?
options: If all circuits are busy, a new call cannot be placed.
If a circuit fails, the call will be forwarded on a new path.
Circuit-switched networks can dynamically learn and use redundant circuits.
A single message can be broken into multiple message blocks that are transmitted through multiple circuits simultaneously.
questions.explanation: In circuit-switched networks, a dedicated circuit is required. If all circuits are busy, a new call cannot be placed.

questions.question: Which expression accurately defines the term congestion?
options: A method of limiting the impact of a hardware or software failure on the network
A measure of the data carrying capacity of the network
A state where the demand on the network resources exceeds the available capacity
A set of techniques to manage the utilization of network resources
questions.explanation: Congestion is the condition where network resource demand exceeds available capacity.

questions.question: Which tool provides real-time video and audio communication over the Internet so that businesses can conduct corporate meetings with participants from several remote locations?
questions.explanation: TelePresence provides real-time video and audio communication for remote meetings.

questions.question: Requiring strong, complex passwords is a practice that supports which network security goal?
questions.explanation: Strong complex passwords help restrict access to authorized users and support data confidentiality.

questions.question: Which three network tools provide the minimum required security protection for home users? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Home users should at minimum use antivirus software, antispyware software, and a firewall.

questions.question: A college is building a new dormitory on its campus. A worker accidentally damages a fiber optic cable that connects two existing dormitories to the campus data center. Although the cable has been cut, students in the dormitories only experience a very short interruption of network services. What characteristic of the network is shown here?
questions.explanation: Fault tolerance allows the network to continue operating or recover quickly when a link or device fails.

questions.question: Which two characters are allowed as part of the hostname of a Cisco device? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Cisco IOS hostnames may include letters, numbers, and dashes. Question marks, spaces, and tabs are not valid hostname characters.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A network administrator is configuring the MOTD on switch SW1. What is the purpose of this command?
questions.imageAlt: Cisco IOS banner motd command configured on switch SW1.
questions.imageCaption: Use the exhibit to answer the question.
options: to display a message when a user accesses the switch
to configure switch SW1 so that only the users in the Admin group can telnet into SW1
to force users of the Admin group to enter a password for authentication
to configure switch SW1 so that the message will display when a user enters the enable command
questions.explanation: The banner motd command displays a message of the day when a user accesses the device.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Based on the test results, which device has connectivity and which device does not have connectivity? (Choose two.)
questions.imageAlt: Network diagram and ping output showing results for 192.168.1.2 and 192.168.1.21.
questions.imageCaption: Use the exhibit to identify the successful and failed connectivity tests.
questions.explanation: The ping to 192.168.1.2, which is switch 2, receives replies. The ping to 192.168.1.21, which is PC-C, times out.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. What three facts can be determined from the show ip interface brief output? (Choose three.)
questions.imageAlt: show ip interface brief output with FastEthernet and VLAN 1 status.
questions.imageCaption: Use the visible command output to select three facts.
options: Two physical interfaces have been configured.
The switch can be remotely managed.
One device is attached to a physical interface.
Passwords have been configured on the switch.
Two devices are attached to the switch.
The default SVI has been configured.
questions.explanation: VLAN 1 has an IP address and is up/up, so the switch can be managed remotely. FastEthernet0/1 is up/up, indicating one active physical connection. The default SVI, VLAN 1, is configured.

questions.question: An administrator is configuring a switch console port with a password. Match the IOS modes in the order the administrator reaches them.
questions.imageAlt: IOS mode order question for configuring the switch console port.
questions.imageCaption: Match each step with the correct IOS mode.
questions.explanation: The order is user EXEC mode, privileged EXEC mode, global configuration mode, and then line configuration mode for line console configuration.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A ping to the default gateway was not successful, but other switches in the same network can ping this gateway. What is a possible reason?
questions.imageAlt: Switch VLAN 1 and default gateway configuration with failed ping output.
questions.imageCaption: Use the configuration and ping output to identify the issue.
options: The VLAN IP address and the default gateway IP address are not in the same network.
The local DNS server is not functioning correctly.
The no shutdown command was not issued for VLAN 1.
The ip default-gateway command has to be issued in the VLAN interface configuration mode.
The default gateway address must be 192.168.10.1.
questions.explanation: The SVI was assigned an IP address, but the exhibit does not show the no shutdown command. If VLAN 1 is administratively down, the switch cannot ping the default gateway.

questions.question: Match the description to the common IOS CLI access method.
questions.imageAlt: Common IOS CLI access methods: console port, virtual interface, and AUX port.
questions.imageCaption: Match each description with the access method.

pairs.left: It displays startup, debugging, and error messages by default.
It can be used to restore an out-of-box configuration on a switch or router.
It allows access through use of Telnet or SSH protocols.
It requires an active network connection.
It is not supported on Catalyst switch devices.

questions.explanation: Console access is local and useful for initial or recovery configuration. Virtual interface access uses the network with Telnet or SSH. AUX access is modem/dialup based and is not supported on Catalyst switches.

questions.question: Which two functions are provided by a network operating system? (Choose two.)
options: Physically forwards bits over copper media
Replaces the need for IP addressing
questions.explanation: A network operating system provides interfaces such as CLI and controls access to device hardware and software resources.

questions.question: Which access method requires a direct physical connection to the device management port?
questions.explanation: Console access uses a direct physical connection to the console port and is commonly used for initial device configuration.

questions.question: What is the purpose of assigning a hostname to a network device?
options: To identify the device in prompts, logs, and documentation
To encrypt all remote management traffic
To replace the device IP address
questions.explanation: A hostname makes the device easier to identify when administering, documenting, and troubleshooting the network.

questions.question: Which command protects privileged EXEC mode on a Cisco IOS device?
questions.explanation: The enable secret command sets an encrypted password for access to privileged EXEC mode.

questions.question: Match each Cisco IOS mode with its prompt.
questions.explanation: Cisco IOS prompts change to show the current command mode.

questions.question: The command ____ saves the running configuration to the startup configuration.
questions.explanation: The running configuration is stored in RAM. Copying it to startup configuration preserves it for the next reload.

questions.question: Which two protocols can provide remote access to the CLI of a Cisco device? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: SSH and Telnet can be used for remote CLI access. SSH is preferred because it encrypts the session.

questions.question: Why should SSH be used instead of Telnet for remote device management?
options: SSH encrypts the remote management session.
SSH requires no username or password.
SSH works only over a console cable.
questions.explanation: SSH encrypts remote management traffic, while Telnet sends data in plaintext.

questions.question: What is the Cisco IOS?
options: The memory for the Cisco network device
The configuration for the Cisco network device
The operating system for the Cisco network device
The CPU for the Cisco network device
questions.explanation: The Cisco IOS (Internetworking Operating System) is the operating system used in most Cisco network devices.

questions.question: What type of connection to a Cisco IOS switch is used to make the initial configuration?
questions.explanation: The initial configuration of Cisco IOS devices is accomplished through the CLI on the console connection.

questions.question: What command will display a list of keywords available for viewing the status of an IOS switch?
questions.explanation: Entering a question mark (?) after a command will show all additional commands and keywords to be used in the command sequence.

questions.question: How is the Cisco IOS generally accessed and navigated?
options: Through the CLI using a terminal emulator
By the use of a custom GUI
questions.explanation: While there are some GUI interfaces available on Cisco IOS-based devices, the current practice is to use the CLI for device configuration and troubleshooting.

questions.question: What is initially entered at the CLI of the Cisco IOS when typing a command sequence?
questions.explanation: The IOS command parser inspects the first entries of a command sequence, expecting to identify a known command.

questions.question: When the command "Switch(config)#hostname EASt-2+56" is entered in a Cisco IOS device using the CLI, what will be returned in the CLI?
questions.explanation: When the device's host name is configured, this name is used verbatim in the CLI prompt.

questions.question: What is the primary defense against unauthorized remote access to network devices?
questions.explanation: Forcing authentication for remote access by requiring a password to remotely connect to a network is a basic security measure. In practice, stronger authentication should be required.

questions.question: Where is the configuration used during startup on Cisco IOS devices located?
questions.explanation: The startup configuration provides the configuration for the operation of the IOS device during startup and is stored in NVRAM.

questions.question:
What is the purpose of the following switch configuration?

s1(config)# interface vlan 1
s1(config-if)# ip address 192.168.122.222 255.255.255.0
s1(config-if)# no shutdown
s1(config-if)# exit
options: Allows communication to manage the switch
Allows the switch to forward traffic
Allows the switch to provide name resolution
questions.explanation: This configuration provides management connectivity to the switch. A switch can forward traffic without this configuration, and name resolution or dynamic host configuration are not provided by these commands.

questions.question: From the CLI of a switch with an address of 192.168.1.44, what command would be used to verify end-to-end connectivity to another host?
questions.explanation: This provides a ping to a remote host. The show ip interface brief command does not verify connectivity, ping 127.0.0.1 verifies the logical IP stack, and ping 192.168.1.44 verifies the local host configuration.

questions.question: In an operating system, which component allocates hardware resources for software processes?
questions.explanation: The kernel manages hardware resources and makes them available to software. The shell is the user-facing interface.

questions.question: Which IOS command moves the user back one level in the command hierarchy?
questions.explanation: The exit command returns to the previous IOS mode. The end command and Ctrl-Z return to privileged EXEC mode.

questions.question: A router has a valid IOS image and a saved configuration in NVRAM, but no console password is configured. Which mode appears after boot?
questions.explanation: With a valid IOS and startup configuration, the device boots to user EXEC mode. Privileged EXEC still requires the enable password or secret.

questions.question: Which two tasks are supported by IOS context-sensitive help? (Choose two.)
options: Showing available commands in the current mode
Showing valid keywords or arguments for a command
questions.explanation: Context-sensitive help lists commands, keywords, and arguments that are valid from the current prompt or command position.

questions.question: What information is shown by the show startup-config command?
options: The IOS image loaded in RAM
The bootstrap code stored in ROM
The active configuration stored in RAM
The saved configuration stored in NVRAM
questions.explanation: show startup-config displays the saved startup configuration in NVRAM. show running-config displays the active configuration in RAM.

questions.question: Which two hostnames follow Cisco IOS naming guidelines? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Cisco device hostnames should start with a letter, contain no spaces, use letters, digits, and hyphens, and end with a letter or digit.

questions.question: What does the service password-encryption command do on a Cisco IOS device?
options: Encrypts passwords stored in the configuration file
Encrypts all packets sent through the device
Requires users to type encrypted text at login
Enables SSH on all VTY lines
questions.explanation: The command hides plaintext passwords in the configuration by storing them in an encrypted form.

questions.question: A technician made unsaved configuration changes that did not fix a problem. What is the cleanest way to discard those running-config changes and return to the saved startup configuration?
questions.explanation: Reloading without saving discards unsaved running-config changes. Copying startup-config to running-config merges settings and may not remove all changes.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the running configuration on a Cisco IOS device?
options: Changes to it affect device operation immediately
It is stored permanently in NVRAM
It is removed with erase running-config
It is saved automatically on every reload
questions.explanation: Commands entered into the running configuration take effect immediately. They must be saved separately to survive a reload.

questions.question: Which two statements about RAM on Cisco devices are true? (Choose two.)
options: The active running configuration is stored in RAM
RAM contents are lost after a power cycle
RAM exists only in switches, not routers
RAM stores multiple IOS images permanently
questions.explanation: RAM stores active operational data such as the running configuration and is volatile, so its contents are lost when power is removed.

questions.question: Which interface is used to remotely manage a Layer 2 switch through an IP address?
questions.explanation: A Layer 2 switch uses a switch virtual interface, or SVI, for IP-based remote management.

questions.question: Which SVI exists by default on a Cisco switch?
questions.explanation: VLAN 1 is the default switch virtual interface. Ethernet interfaces are physical ports, and VLAN 99 must be created or configured.

questions.question: Why is an IP address configured on a Layer 2 switch?
options: To let the switch send broadcasts
To make the switch a default gateway
To let the switch receive Ethernet frames
questions.explanation: Layer 2 switching does not require an IP address, but remote management through the network does.

questions.question: Which Windows command displays the current IP configuration of a PC?
questions.explanation: ipconfig displays IP addressing information on Windows. The show commands are Cisco IOS commands.

questions.question: A newly connected PC reaches the network without manual IP settings. What is the most likely reason?
options: The PC does not need IP addressing
The factory permanently assigned the correct LAN address
The PC is configured to use DHCP
DNS automatically assigned the IP address
questions.explanation: A DHCP client can automatically receive an IP address, subnet mask, gateway, and other settings from a DHCP server.

questions.question: What is a user testing by pinging a remote IP address such as 10.1.1.1?
options: Whether the local TCP/IP stack works without network traffic
Whether the destination can be reached
What hardware model exists at the destination
questions.explanation: A ping to a destination address tests basic IP connectivity to that destination.

questions.question: Before selecting IOS images for upgrades, which three details should an administrator verify? (Choose three.)
options: Whether all devices are on the same LAN
The installed router and switch ports
Whether every device has the same hostname
questions.explanation: IOS image selection depends on device model, hardware resources such as RAM and flash, and the feature set required.

questions.question: After service password-encryption is enabled, what changes when the configuration is viewed?
options: Plaintext passwords are no longer displayed as clear text
Only the enable secret is removed
Users must enter encrypted strings to log in
questions.explanation: The command obfuscates plaintext passwords in the displayed configuration so they are not shown directly.

questions.question: What is a quick way to test whether an MOTD banner is displayed correctly?
options: Press Ctrl-Z at privileged EXEC mode
Leave privileged EXEC mode and press Enter
questions.explanation: The MOTD banner is shown when a user accesses the device. Exiting the session context and pressing Enter can trigger the login/banner display without a reboot.

questions.question: Which three IOS access areas can commonly be protected with passwords? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Passwords are commonly applied to console access, VTY remote access, and privileged EXEC access.

questions.question: What benefit does DHCP provide for hosts on a network?
options: Hosts always keep the same address
Users can browse by name instead of IP address
Hosts can receive IP settings automatically
questions.explanation: DHCP automatically assigns IP configuration to hosts. It does not guarantee the same address forever or replace DNS.

questions.question: When designing IPv4 addressing for end devices, which rule must be followed?
options: Each address must match a DNS-assigned value
Each address must be unique in the local network
Each address must be compatible with the MAC address
Each host must use a different network portion
questions.explanation: Host IP addresses must be unique within the local network. They are independent of MAC addresses and are not assigned by DNS.

questions.question: Which two statements describe flash memory on Cisco devices? (Choose two.)
options: Flash receives a copy of IOS from RAM at boot
Flash contents are lost at each power cycle
questions.explanation: Flash is nonvolatile memory and can store IOS images or other files that may be overwritten.

questions.question: Match each IOS shortcut with its function.

pairs.right: Completes an abbreviated command or keyword
Displays the next screen of output
Interrupts a process such as ping or traceroute

matchOptions: Completes an abbreviated command or keyword
Displays the next screen of output
Interrupts a process such as ping or traceroute
questions.explanation: IOS includes editing and help shortcuts that make command entry and output navigation faster.

questions.question: Match each IOS access method with its description.

pairs.right: Local access that displays startup, debugging, and error messages by default
Remote access through protocols such as Telnet or SSH
Access method associated with dialup connections and not supported on Catalyst switches

matchOptions: Local access that displays startup, debugging, and error messages by default
Remote access through protocols such as Telnet or SSH
Access method associated with dialup connections and not supported on Catalyst switches
Physical interface used only for Ethernet frame forwarding
Protocol used to automatically assign IP addresses
questions.explanation: Console, virtual terminal, and AUX access methods are used for different local or remote management scenarios.

questions.question: A remote worker logs in with credentials, uses video conferencing, and an ISP failure is hidden by a backup link. Which three network characteristics are shown? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Credentials relate to security, good video experience relates to QoS, and backup connectivity relates to fault tolerance.

questions.question: What happens after ipv6 unicast-routing is configured globally on an IPv6-capable router?
options: All router interfaces are automatically enabled
IPv6-enabled interfaces can send ICMPv6 Router Advertisement messages
Every interface receives a global unicast address automatically
A static global IPv6 address is created on the router
questions.explanation: The ipv6 unicast-routing command enables IPv6 routing behavior, including router advertisements on IPv6-enabled interfaces.

questions.question: Which two ICMPv6 message types are additions compared with ICMP for IPv4? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: ICMPv6 includes Neighbor Solicitation and Router Advertisement messages used by IPv6 neighbor discovery and router discovery.

questions.question: Which two details appear in show ip interface brief output? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: show ip interface brief lists interface IP addresses and interface status information, including physical layer status.

questions.question: A packet sent to a server uses destination TCP port 80. Which service is being requested?
questions.explanation: TCP port 80 is the well-known port for HTTP web traffic.

questions.question: What are the purpose and functions of the physical layer in data networks? (Choose two.)
options: Controls how the data is transmitted onto the physical media
questions.explanation: The physical layer controls data transmitted onto the media and provides encoding of the bits. Logical addressing is provided by Layer 3. Packaging bits into data units and media access control are provided by the data link layer.

questions.question: Which of these statements regarding UTP network cabling are true? (Choose two.)
options: Most difficult type of networking cable to install
Most commonly used type of networking cable
questions.explanation: UTP cabling uses twisted copper pairs. The twists provide some rejection of stray electrical and magnetic signals, but UTP is still susceptible to EMI and RFI. Because of its relatively low cost and good performance, UTP is the most common networking media in use.

questions.question: What is the purpose of cladding in fiber-optic cables?
questions.explanation: Cladding is the glass that surrounds the fiber core and reflects light pulses back into the core. This keeps the light contained in the fiber through total internal reflection.

questions.question: Identify the wire colors associated with the pins when building a 568B network cable.
questions.explanation: The 568B pinout from pin 1 to pin 8 is orange-white, orange, green-white, blue, blue-white, green, brown-white, and brown.

questions.question: What are the advantages of using fiber-optic cable over copper cable? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Fiber-optic cable can transmit signals with less attenuation than copper, is immune to EMI and RFI, supports longer cable runs, and has greater bandwidth potential.

questions.question: What occurs when another wireless device connects to a wireless access point (WAP)?
options: The WAP adds an additional channel to support the new client.
The WAP throughput for all the connected clients decreases.
The WAP decreases the radio coverage area.
The WAP will change frequencies to reduce interference caused by the new client.
questions.explanation: Wireless devices share access to the same airwaves when connecting to a WAP. As more wireless devices access the network at the same time, throughput available to clients can decrease.

questions.question: If a node receives a frame and the calculated CRC does not match the CRC in the FCS, what action will the node take?
options: Reconstruct the frame from the CRC
Forward the frame as it is to the next host
Disable the interface on which the frame arrives
questions.explanation: The receiving node calculates its own CRC and compares it with the CRC in the FCS. If the values do not match, the frame is considered corrupted and is discarded.

questions.question: What are the contents of the data field in a frame?
questions.explanation: The Layer 3 PDU is encapsulated with a Layer 2 header and trailer to form the Layer 2 frame. The frame data field contains the network layer PDU.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the logical topology of a network?
options: Is determined by how the nodes in the network are connected
Defines how frames are transferred from one node to the next
questions.explanation: Logical topology describes how a network transfers frames from one node to the next. It is about the data path, not necessarily the physical layout.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of contention-based MAC?
options: Nodes compete for the use of the medium.
Leaves MAC to the upper layer.
Each node has a specific time to use the medium.
questions.explanation: In contention-based access, all nodes compete for use of the medium and follow rules for handling collisions or contention.

questions.question: What are two reasons physical layer protocols use frame encoding techniques? (Choose two.)
options: To reduce collisions on the media
To provide better media error correction
To identify where a frame starts and ends
To distinguish data information from control information
questions.explanation: Encoding uses predefined signal patterns that help receivers recognize frame boundaries and distinguish data information from control information.

questions.question: What does throughput indicate?
options: The guaranteed rate offered by an ISP
The capacity of a medium to carry data
The usable application data transferred across the media
The bits transferred across the media over a given period of time
The time needed for a message to reach the destination
questions.explanation: Throughput measures the actual transfer of bits across the media during a period of time. Goodput is the portion of throughput that is usable application data.

questions.question: New Ethernet cabling near fluorescent lights and electrical equipment carries corrupted data. Which two factors can interfere with copper cabling? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic interference and radio frequency interference can distort copper cable signals. Crosstalk comes from adjacent wires, and attenuation is signal weakening over distance.

questions.question: Which characteristic describes crosstalk?
options: Distortion caused by signals carried in adjacent wires
Weakening of a signal over long cable lengths
Loss of wireless signal because of distance from an access point
questions.explanation: Crosstalk is interference caused when the electric or magnetic field of a signal on one wire affects a signal on an adjacent wire.

questions.question: What UTP cable technique helps protect against crosstalk?
options: Wrapping foil around the wire pairs
Terminating the cable with grounded connectors
questions.explanation: UTP pairs are twisted so the magnetic fields generated by the wires tend to cancel each other, reducing crosstalk.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. The PC is connected to the switch console port. All other links are FastEthernet. Which UTP cable types connect the devices?
questions.imageAlt: A PC connected to a switch, then to a router, then to another router, with links labeled 1, 2, and 3.
questions.imageCaption: Identify the cable type for each numbered link.
questions.explanation: A rollover cable is used for console access. Straight-through cable is used between unlike Ethernet devices such as switch to router. Crossover cable is used between similar devices such as router to router.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. What is wrong with the displayed cable termination?
questions.imageAlt: An RJ-45 termination with too much untwisted wire visible before the connector.
questions.imageCaption: Inspect the termination shown in the exhibit.
options: The woven copper braid should not have been removed.
The wrong type of connector is being used.
The untwisted length of each wire is too long.
The wires are too thick for the connector.
questions.explanation: When terminating an RJ-45 connector, the untwisted wire length should be kept short and the cable jacket should be crimped by the connector.

questions.question: Which connector type is used by a typical Ethernet network interface card?
questions.explanation: Ethernet NICs commonly use RJ-45 connectors for twisted-pair copper cabling.

questions.question: What is one advantage of fiber-optic cabling over copper cabling?
options: It is usually cheaper than copper cabling.
It can be installed around sharp bends.
It is easier to terminate and install than copper cabling.
It can carry signals much farther than copper cabling.
questions.explanation: Fiber-optic cable generally supports longer distances than copper cable and is also immune to EMI and RFI.

questions.question: Why are two strands of fiber used for a single fiber-optic connection?
options: To allow data to travel longer distances without degrading
To increase the speed of light in the fiber
questions.explanation: Light travels in one direction through a fiber strand, so two strands are used to support simultaneous sending and receiving.

questions.question: Which three areas should be considered when designing a wireless network? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Wireless design must account for coverage, interference sources, and security. Extensive cabling is not a primary wireless design concern.

questions.question: Which OSI layer specifies the encapsulation method used for different media types?
questions.explanation: The data link layer defines framing and encapsulation for different physical media types.

questions.question: What are two services performed by the OSI data link layer? (Choose two.)
options: Determines the path for forwarding packets
Accepts Layer 3 packets and encapsulates them into frames
Provides media access control and error detection
Builds a MAC address table for all Layer 2 communication
questions.explanation: The data link layer encapsulates Layer 3 packets into frames and provides media access control and error detection over the local media.

questions.question: Which statement is true about physical and logical topologies?
options: The logical topology is always the same as the physical topology.
Physical topologies describe how frames are transferred.
Physical topologies display the IP addressing scheme.
Logical topologies describe how data transfers between devices.
questions.explanation: Physical topology shows device interconnection. Logical topology describes the path and method used to transfer data between nodes.

questions.question: Which data transfer method allows information to be sent and received at the same time?
questions.explanation: Full-duplex communication allows both devices to transmit and receive simultaneously.

questions.question: Which statement describes an extended star topology?
options: End devices connect to a central device, which connects to other central devices.
End devices are connected on a bus and each bus connects to a central device.
Each end system connects to a neighbor through an intermediate device.
All devices are connected in a single chain.
questions.explanation: In an extended star, central intermediate devices connect multiple star topologies together.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Which statement describes the media access control methods used by the networks?
questions.imageAlt: A diagram with Network 1 as an Ethernet LAN, Network 2 as a point-to-point link, and Network 3 as a wireless LAN.
questions.imageCaption: Compare the access methods used by the three networks.
options: None of the networks require media access control.
Network 1 uses CSMA/CD and Network 3 uses CSMA/CA.
Network 1 uses CSMA/CA and Network 2 uses CSMA/CD.
Network 2 uses CSMA/CA and Network 3 uses CSMA/CD.
questions.explanation: The wired Ethernet LAN uses CSMA/CD, the point-to-point WAN does not require contention-based access, and the WLAN uses CSMA/CA.

questions.question: What is contained in the trailer of a data-link frame?
questions.explanation: The frame trailer contains error detection information, commonly in the FCS field.

questions.question: As data travels on media as 1s and 0s, how does a receiving node identify the beginning and end of a frame?
options: The transmitting node inserts start and stop indicators into the frame.
The transmitting node sends a beacon before every frame.
The receiving node identifies the frame by seeing a physical address first.
The transmitting node sends an out-of-band signal to mark the frame.
questions.explanation: The framing process inserts start and stop indicators so the receiver can detect frame boundaries.

questions.question: What is a role of the Logical Link Control sublayer?
options: Provides access to Layer 1 network technologies
Defines media access processes performed by hardware
Marks frames to identify the network layer protocol being carried
questions.explanation: LLC communicates with the network layer and identifies which Layer 3 protocol is encapsulated in a frame.

questions.question: What is the definition of bandwidth?
options: The usable data transferred over a given period
The speed at which bits travel on a network
The measured bits transferred across the media during a period
The amount of data that can flow from one place to another in a given time
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the capacity of a medium to carry data between two points during a specific amount of time.

questions.question: What is the function of the CRC value in the FCS field of a frame?
options: To verify the integrity of the received frame
To verify the physical address in the frame
To verify the logical address in the frame
To compute the checksum header for the data field
questions.explanation: The receiver compares the CRC in the FCS with its own computed CRC. If they differ, the frame is discarded.

questions.question: The term ____ indicates the capacity of a medium to carry data and is typically measured in kb/s or Mb/s.
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the data-carrying capacity of a medium, usually measured in bits per second and its multiples.

questions.question: What acronym identifies the data link sublayer that identifies the network layer protocol encapsulated in a frame?
questions.explanation: Logical Link Control, or LLC, places information in the frame to identify the encapsulated network layer protocol.

questions.question: Match each characteristic to the correct fiber type.
questions.imageAlt: Fiber type matching exhibit with multimode and single-mode fiber targets.
questions.imageCaption: Not every visible option is used.

pairs.left: Several paths of light into the fiber
Only one ray of light into the fiber

questions.explanation: Multimode fiber uses LEDs, supports multiple light paths, and is common in LANs. Single-mode fiber uses laser light, has one primary light path, and is common for campus backbone links.

questions.question: A physical topology that combines point-to-point, hub-and-spoke, or mesh designs is commonly known as a ____ topology.
questions.explanation: A hybrid topology is a variation or combination of other topology types, such as partial mesh or extended star.

questions.question: What are two examples of hybrid topologies? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Partial mesh and extended star are hybrid topologies because they combine or vary other topology patterns.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes signaling at the physical layer?
options: Asynchronous signals are transmitted without a clock signal.
A 1 always means voltage and a 0 always means no voltage.
Wireless encoding sends clicks to delimit frames.
Signaling converts a stream of data into a predefined code.
questions.explanation: Asynchronous signaling does not use a shared clock signal. Converting data into predefined code patterns describes encoding.

questions.question: A FastEthernet network has 80 Mb/s throughput and 15 Mb/s of overhead. What is the goodput?
questions.explanation: Goodput is throughput minus overhead. 80 Mb/s minus 15 Mb/s equals 65 Mb/s.

questions.question: How is the magnetic field cancellation effect enhanced in UTP cables?
options: By increasing the PVC sheath thickness
By increasing and varying the number of twists in each wire pair
By decreasing the number of wires used to carry data
questions.explanation: Different twist rates in UTP pairs improve cancellation of magnetic fields and reduce crosstalk.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about multimode fiber?
options: It carries signals from multiple connected sending devices.
It commonly uses a laser as a light source.
SC-SC patch cords can be used with multimode fiber cables.
It has a thinner core than single-mode fiber.
questions.explanation: Multimode fiber commonly uses LED light and has a larger core than single-mode fiber. SC connectors can be used on multimode fiber patch cords.

questions.question: A network administrator must upgrade wireless access to support up to 1.3 Gb/s while remaining backward compatible. Which wireless standard should be implemented?
questions.explanation: 802.11ac supports data rates up to the gigabit range, including 1.3 Gb/s, and remains backward compatible with earlier Wi-Fi standards in supported bands.

questions.question: What is one main characteristic of the data link layer?
options: It generates electrical or optical signals for 1s and 0s.
It converts data bits into predefined code.
It shields upper layer protocols from the physical medium details.
It accepts Layer 3 packets and decides the path to remote networks.
questions.explanation: The data link layer allows upper layers to operate without needing to know the details of the physical medium being used.

questions.question: What are two characteristics of 802.11 wireless networks? (Choose two.)
options: Stations can transmit at any time.
Collisions can exist in the networks.
questions.explanation: 802.11 wireless networks use CSMA/CA to reduce collisions, but collisions can still occur because wireless stations share the medium.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the FCS field in a frame?
options: To obtain the MAC address of the sender
To verify the logical address of the sender
To compute the CRC header for the data field
To determine whether errors occurred during transmission and reception
questions.explanation: The FCS stores error detection information used by the receiver to determine whether the frame was corrupted.

questions.question: 10,000,000,000 b/s can also be written as ____ Gb/s.
questions.explanation: One gigabit per second equals one billion bits per second, so 10,000,000,000 b/s equals 10 Gb/s.

questions.question: Match the steps to the physical layer operations that occur when data is sent from one node and received at another.
questions.imageAlt: Physical layer operation sequence matching exhibit.
questions.imageCaption: Match each step with the correct operation.

pairs.right: The physical layer encodes the frames.
The physical layer creates the signals that represent the bits in each frame.
The signals are sent on the media one at a time.
The physical layer retrieves the individual signals from the media.
The physical layer restores the individual signals to their bit representations.

matchOptions: The physical layer encodes the frames.
The physical layer creates the signals that represent the bits in each frame.
The signals are sent on the media one at a time.
The physical layer retrieves the individual signals from the media.
The physical layer restores the individual signals to their bit representations.
The physical layer passes the packets up to the internet layer.
questions.explanation: The physical layer encodes frames, creates signals, transmits them over the media, retrieves the signals at the receiver, and restores them to bit representations.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Which statement describes the media access control methods used by the networks?
questions.imageAlt: A diagram with Network 1 as an Ethernet LAN, Network 2 as a point-to-point link, and Network 3 as a wireless LAN.
questions.imageCaption: Compare the access methods used by the three networks.
options: None of the networks require media access control.
Network 1 uses CSMA/CD and Network 3 uses CSMA/CA.
Network 1 uses CSMA/CA and Network 2 uses CSMA/CD.
Network 2 uses CSMA/CA and Network 3 uses CSMA/CD.
questions.explanation: Network 1 is wired Ethernet and uses CSMA/CD. Network 2 is point-to-point. Network 3 is wireless and uses CSMA/CA.

questions.question: What happens to a port that is associated with VLAN 10 when the administrator deletes VLAN 10 from the switch?
options: The port creates the VLAN again.
The port goes back to the default VLAN.
The port automatically associates itself with the native VLAN.
questions.explanation: If the VLAN that is associated with a port is deleted, the port becomes inactive and cannot communicate with the network any more. To verify that a port is in an inactive state, use the show interfaces switchport command.

questions.question: In which memory location are the VLAN configurations of normal range VLANs stored on a Catalyst switch?
questions.explanation: When a normal range VLAN is created the configuration information of the VLAN is stored in flash in the vlan.dat file.

questions.question: An administrator is investigating a failure on a trunk link between a Cisco switch and a switch from another vendor. After a few show commands, the administrator notices that the switches are not negotiating a trunk. What is a probable cause for this issue?
options: Both switches are in nonegotiate mode.
Switches from other vendors do not support DTP.
Both switches are in trunk mode.
DTP frames are flooding the entire network.
questions.explanation: DTP is a Cisco proprietary protocol. Non-Cisco switches do not support DTP.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the vlan.dat file on a switch?
questions.explanation: The VLAN database (vlan.dat) contains information about normal range VLANs such as the VLAN number, name, and VTP mode.

questions.question: What is the purpose of setting the native VLAN separate from data VLANs?
options: A separate VLAN should be used to carry uncommon untagged frames to avoid bandwidth contention on data VLANS.
The security of management frames that are carried in the native VLAN can be enhanced.
The native VLAN is for carrying VLAN management traffic only.
The native VLAN is for routers and switches to exchange their management information, so it should be different from data VLANS.
questions.explanation: When a Cisco switch trunk port receives untagged frames, it forwards these frames to the native VLAN. When the native VLAN is moved away from data VLANs, those untagged frames will not compete for bandwidth in the data VLANs. The native VLAN is not designed for carrying management traffic, but rather is for backward compatibility with legacy LAN scenarios.

questions.question: When a Cisco switch receives untagged frames on a 802.1Q trunk port, which VLAN ID is the traffic switched to by default?
questions.explanation: A native VLAN is used to forward untagged frames that are received on a Cisco switch 802.1Q trunk port. Untagged frames that are received on a trunk port are not forwarded to any other VLAN except the native VLAN.

questions.question: A network administrator is determining the best placement of VLAN trunk links. Which two types of point-to-point connections utilize VLAN trunking?
options: between two switches that utilize multiple VLANs
between a switch and a server that has an 802.1Q NIC
between a switch and a network printer
between two switches that share a common VLAN
between a switch and a client PC
questions.explanation: VLAN trunk links are used to allow VLAN traffic to propagate between devices such as switches, routers, and servers that support 802.1Q tagging.

questions.question: What are three primary benefits of using VLANs?
options: a reduction in the number of trunk links
questions.explanation: Security, cost reduction, and improved IT staff efficiency are benefits of using VLANs, along with higher performance, broadcast storm mitigation, and simpler project and application management.

questions.question: On a Cisco switch, where is extended range VLAN information stored?
questions.explanation: Extended range VLANs, 1006 through 4094, are not written to the vlan.dat file but are saved in the running configuration file.

questions.question: In which location are the normal range VLANs stored on a Cisco switch by default?
questions.explanation: Normal range VLANs are stored in a file called vlan.dat and located in the flash memory.

questions.question: Which distinct type of VLAN is used by an administrator to access and configure a switch?
questions.explanation: A management VLAN is used to remotely access and configure a switch.

questions.question: For what reason would a network administrator use the show interfaces trunk command on a switch?
options: to examine DTP negotiation as it occurs
to display an IP address for any existing VLAN
to verify port association with a particular VLAN
questions.explanation: The show interfaces trunk command displays trunk ports, trunking mode, encapsulation type, trunk status, native VLAN, and allowed VLANs on the link.

questions.question: Where is the vlan.dat file stored on a switch?
options: on the externally attached storage media or internal hard drive
questions.explanation: Normal range VLAN configurations are stored within a VLAN database file, called vlan.dat, which is located in the flash memory of the switch.

questions.question: If an organization is changing to include Cisco IP phones in its network, what design feature must be considered to ensure voice quality?
options: Voice traffic needs to be tagged with the native VLAN.
A separate VLAN is needed for voice traffic.
Voice traffic and data traffic require separate trunk links between switches.
Additional switch ports that are dedicated to Cisco IP phones are required.
questions.explanation: Voice traffic cannot tolerate much packet delay, so it needs to be in a separate VLAN. The voice VLAN can be configured to provide QoS.

questions.question: A Cisco switch currently allows traffic tagged with VLANs 10 and 20 across trunk port Fa0/5. What is the effect of issuing a switchport trunk allowed vlan 30 command on Fa0/5?
options: It allows a native VLAN of 30 to be implemented on Fa0/5.
It allows VLANs 10, 20, and 30 on Fa0/5.
It allows only VLAN 30 on Fa0/5.
It allows VLANs 1 to 30 on Fa0/5.
questions.explanation: The switchport trunk allowed vlan 30 command allows only traffic tagged with VLAN 30 across the trunk port. Any VLAN that is not specified in this command will not be allowed on this trunk port.

questions.question: Which three statements accurately describe VLAN types?
options: A data VLAN is used to carry VLAN management data and user-generated traffic.
A management VLAN is any VLAN that is configured to access management features of the switch.
After the initial boot of an unconfigured switch, all ports are members of the default VLAN.
An 802.1Q trunk port, with a native VLAN assigned, supports both tagged and untagged traffic.
Voice VLANs are used to support user phone and email traffic on a network.
VLAN 1 is always used as the management VLAN.
questions.explanation: A management VLAN is configured to manage features of the switch. By default, all ports are members of the default VLAN. An 802.1Q trunk port supports both tagged and untagged traffic.

questions.question: Which type of VLAN is used to designate which traffic is untagged when crossing a trunk port?
questions.explanation: A native VLAN is the VLAN that does not receive a VLAN tag in the IEEE 802.1Q frame header.

questions.question: What are two primary benefits of using VLANs?
options: A reduction in the number of trunk links
questions.explanation: Cost reduction and improved IT staff efficiency are benefits of using VLANs, along with higher performance, broadcast storm mitigation, and simpler project and application management.

questions.question: Which command displays the encapsulation type, the voice VLAN ID, and the access mode VLAN for the Fa0/1 interface?
questions.explanation: The show interfaces switchport command displays switchport mode, trunking encapsulation, access mode VLAN, native VLAN, and voice VLAN information.

questions.question: What must the network administrator do to remove FastEthernet 0/1 from VLAN 2 and assign it to VLAN 3?
options: Enter the no shutdown interface config command on Fa0/1.
Enter the no vlan 2 and the vlan 3 global config commands.
Enter the switchport access vlan 3 interface config command on Fa0/1.
Enter the switchport trunk native vlan 3 interface config command on Fa0/1.
questions.explanation: Entering the switchport access vlan 3 interface configuration command on Fa0/1 replaces the current port VLAN assignment from VLAN 2 to VLAN 3.

questions.question: A Cisco Catalyst switch has been added to support the use of multiple VLANs as part of an enterprise network. The network technician finds it necessary to clear all VLAN information from the switch in order to incorporate a new network design. What should the technician do to accomplish this task?
options: Delete the IP address that is assigned to the management VLAN and reboot the switch.
Delete the startup configuration and the vlan.dat file in the flash memory of the switch and reboot the switch.
Erase the running configuration and reboot the switch.
Erase the startup configuration and reboot the switch.
questions.explanation: To restore a Catalyst switch to factory default condition, erase the startup configuration, delete vlan.dat, and reboot the switch.

questions.question: Which two characteristics match extended range VLANs?
options: CDP can be used to learn and store these VLANs.
They are commonly used in small networks.
They are saved in the running-config file by default.
VLANs are initialized from flash memory.
questions.explanation: Extended range VLANs are stored in the running configuration file by default and use VLAN IDs from 1006 to 4094.

questions.question: What happens to switch ports after the VLAN to which they are assigned is deleted?
options: The ports are assigned to VLAN 1, the default VLAN.
The ports are disabled and must be re-enabled using the no shutdown command.
The ports are placed in trunk mode.
The ports stop communicating with the attached devices.
questions.explanation: Any ports that are not moved to an active VLAN cannot communicate with other hosts after the VLAN is deleted. They must be assigned to an active VLAN or their VLAN must be recreated.

questions.question: You must configure a trunk link between a Cisco Catalyst 2960 switch and another vendor Layer 2 switch. Which two commands should be configured to enable the trunk link?
questions.explanation: To enable trunking from a Cisco switch to a device that does not support DTP, use switchport mode trunk and switchport nonegotiate. This makes the interface a trunk and prevents DTP frames.

questions.question: A PC is to access a web server on another network. Which inter-VLAN method will provide the highest bandwidth at Layer 3 and also provide a default gateway for the PC?
options: trunked interface between the router and the switch
multiple physical interfaces on the router, all connected to a Layer 2 switch
questions.explanation: A router-on-a-stick design is the same as having a trunked interface between the router and the switch. It works, but does not scale well because all VLANs traverse one connection. Multiple router interfaces can be faster, but routers have limited physical interfaces. Layer 3 switches with routing enabled have more Ethernet ports and can route in hardware.

questions.question: Which scalable method must be implemented in order to provide inter-VLAN routing on a switched network with more than 1000 VLANs?
options: routing traffic internally to a Layer 3 switch device
configuring static routes on a Layer 2 switch device
connecting a router interface to a switch port that is configured in trunk mode to route packets between VLANs, with each VLAN assigned to a router subinterface
connecting each physical router interface to a different physical switch port, with each switch port assigned to a different VLAN
questions.explanation: Multilayer switching is the most scalable inter-VLAN routing method because traffic is routed internally by the switch device. Router-on-a-stick and legacy inter-VLAN routing do not scale well for very large numbers of VLANs.

questions.question: When configuring a router as part of a router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing topology, where should the IP address be assigned?
questions.explanation: The IP address and encapsulation type should be assigned to each router subinterface in a router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN topology.

questions.question: A small college uses VLAN 10 for the classroom network and VLAN 20 for the office network. What is needed to enable communication between these two VLANs while using legacy inter-VLAN routing?
options: Two groups of switches are needed, each with ports that are configured for one VLAN.
A router with at least two LAN interfaces should be used.
A router with one VLAN interface is needed to connect to the SVI on a switch.
A switch with a port that is configured as trunk is needed to connect to a router.
questions.explanation: With legacy inter-VLAN routing, different physical router interfaces connect to different physical switch ports. The switch ports connected to the router are access ports, each assigned to a different VLAN.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of using multilayer switches for inter-VLAN routing?
options: Multilayer switches are more expensive than router-on-a-stick implementations.
Multilayer switches have higher latency for Layer 3 routing.
Spanning tree must be disabled in order to implement routing on a multilayer switch.
Multilayer switches are limited to using trunk links for Layer 3 routing.
questions.explanation: The main disadvantage of multilayer switches is higher cost. Because both routing and switching are done in hardware, multilayer switches are faster than router-on-a-stick.

questions.question: Which type of inter-VLAN communication design requires the configuration of multiple subinterfaces?
questions.explanation: The router-on-a-stick design uses subinterfaces on a router. A multilayer switch uses SVIs instead, and legacy inter-VLAN routing uses physical router interfaces.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of using router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing?
options: does not scale well beyond 50 VLANs
requires the use of more physical interfaces than legacy inter-VLAN routing
requires the use of multiple router interfaces configured to operate as access links
questions.explanation: Router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing does not scale well beyond about 50 VLANs. It uses one router interface as a trunk link and supports VLAN-tagged packets.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the number 10 in the encapsulation dot1Q 10 native router subinterface command?
questions.explanation: The encapsulation command specifies the encapsulation type, the VLAN ID, and optionally the native VLAN. In this command, 10 is the VLAN ID.

questions.question: While configuring inter-VLAN routing on a multilayer switch, a network administrator issues the no switchport command on an interface that is connected to another switch. What is the purpose of this command?
options: to create a switched virtual interface
to create a routed port for a single network
to provide a static trunk link
to provide an access link that tags VLAN traffic
questions.explanation: When a Layer 2 interface on a multilayer switch is configured with no switchport, it becomes a routed port. A routed port can be configured with an IP address for a specific subnet.

questions.question:
A network administrator enters the following command sequence on a Cisco 3560 switch. What is the purpose of these commands?

Switch(config)# interface gigabitethernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
options: to enable the Gi0/1 port as a switch virtual interface
to enable the Gi0/1 port as a bridge virtual interface
to make the Gi0/1 port a routed port
to shut down the Gi0/1 port
questions.explanation: By default, physical ports on a 3560 switch are Layer 2 interfaces. The no switchport command changes the port into a routed Layer 3 port.

questions.question: What operational mode should be used on a switch port to connect it to a router for router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing?
questions.explanation: For router-on-a-stick, the switch port connected to the router must operate as a trunk. Routers do not support DTP, and access mode is used to connect hosts.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly describes the SVI inter-VLAN routing method?
options: A physical interface is needed for every VLAN that is created.
An SVI is needed for each VLAN.
The encapsulation type must be configured on the SVI.
questions.explanation: To create SVI inter-VLAN routing on a Layer 3 switch, the VLAN must exist in the database and an SVI must be explicitly created for each VLAN.

questions.question: How is traffic routed between multiple VLANs on a multilayer switch?
options: Traffic is routed via internal VLAN interfaces.
Traffic is routed via physical interfaces.
Traffic is broadcast out all physical interfaces.
questions.explanation: Multilayer switches perform inter-VLAN routing by using internal VLAN interfaces. Subinterfaces are used on routers, not on multilayer switches for inter-VLAN routing.

questions.question: What is required to perform router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing?
options: a router that is configured with multiple subinterfaces
a router with multiple physical interfaces
a Layer 2 switch that is configured with multiple trunk ports
questions.explanation: Router-on-a-stick uses a single physical router interface configured with multiple subinterfaces, one for each VLAN that will be routed.

questions.question: An administrator was troubleshooting a router-on-a-stick topology and concluded that the problem was related to the configuration of VLANs on the router subinterfaces. Which two commands can the administrator use in the router to identify the problem?
questions.explanation: The show ip interface and show running-config commands can help troubleshoot router subinterface issues such as incorrect VLAN IDs. The other commands do not display the needed subinterface VLAN information.

questions.question: A router has two FastEthernet interfaces and needs to connect to four VLANs in the local network. How can this be accomplished using the fewest number of physical interfaces without unnecessarily decreasing network performance?
options: Add a second router to handle the inter-VLAN traffic.
Interconnect the VLANs via the two additional FastEthernet interfaces.
Use a hub to connect the four VLANS with a FastEthernet interface on the router.
questions.explanation: Legacy inter-VLAN routing for four VLANs would require four physical interfaces. The best router-based solution using the fewest physical interfaces is router-on-a-stick.

questions.question: What distinguishes traditional legacy inter-VLAN routing from router-on-a-stick?
options: Traditional routing is able to use only a single switch interface, whereas a router-on-a-stick can use multiple switch interfaces.
Traditional routing requires a routing protocol, whereas a router-on-a-stick only needs to route directly connected networks.
Traditional routing uses one port per logical network, whereas a router-on-a-stick uses subinterfaces to connect multiple logical networks to a single router port.
Traditional routing uses multiple paths to the router and therefore requires STP, whereas router-on-a-stick does not provide multiple connections and therefore eliminates the need for STP.
