questions.explanation: Traditional inter-VLAN routing uses one physical router port per VLAN. Router-on-a-stick uses subinterfaces to connect multiple logical networks to a single physical router port.

questions.question: Subinterface G0/1.10 on R1 must be configured as the default gateway for the VLAN 10 192.168.10.0/24 network. Which command should be configured on the subinterface to enable inter-VLAN routing for VLAN 10?
questions.explanation: The subinterface must be assigned to VLAN 10 using the encapsulation dot1q 10 command. The switchport commands are switch configuration commands, and encapsulation vlan 10 is not valid.

questions.question: What is important to consider while configuring the subinterfaces of a router when implementing inter-VLAN routing?
options: The IP address of each subinterface must be the default gateway address for each VLAN subnet.
The no shutdown command must be given on each subinterface.
The physical interface must have an IP address configured.
The subinterface numbers must match the VLAN ID number.
questions.explanation: Hosts in each VLAN need a default gateway. The router subinterface IP address should be configured as the default gateway address for that VLAN subnet.

questions.question: What are the steps that must be completed in order to enable inter-VLAN routing using router-on-a-stick?
options: Configure the physical interfaces on the router and enable a routing protocol.
Create the VLANs on the router and define the port membership assignments on the switch.
Create the VLANs on the switch to include port membership assignment and enable a routing protocol on the router.
Create the VLANs on the switch to include port membership assignment and configure subinterfaces on the router matching the VLANs.
questions.explanation: For router-on-a-stick, create the VLANs and port memberships on the switch, configure the switch port to the router as a trunk, and configure router subinterfaces that match the VLANs.

questions.question: What two statements are true regarding the use of subinterfaces for inter-VLAN routing?
options: Fewer router Ethernet ports required than in traditional inter-VLAN routing
Less complex physical connection than in traditional inter-VLAN routing
More switch ports required than in traditional inter-VLAN routing
Simpler Layer 3 troubleshooting than with traditional inter-VLAN routing
Subinterfaces have no contention for bandwidth
questions.explanation: Traditional inter-VLAN routing requires more physical ports and connections. Router-on-a-stick with subinterfaces requires fewer router Ethernet ports and has a less complex physical connection.

questions.question: Which router-on-a-stick command and prompt on R1 correctly encapsulates 802.1Q traffic for VLAN 20?
questions.explanation: The encapsulation dot1q vlan_id [native] command is configured in subinterface configuration mode. Therefore the correct prompt and command are R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1q 20.

questions.question: What are two disadvantages of using the router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing method in a large network?
options: It requires multiple physical interfaces on a router.
It requires subinterfaces to be configured on the same subnets.
questions.explanation: Router-on-a-stick requires a router to route traffic between VLANs and does not scale easily in large networks. Multiple subinterfaces can also affect traffic flow speed, so large networks typically use Layer 3 switches.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of a routed port on a Layer 3 switch?
options: It requires the switchport mode access interface config command.
It requires the no switchport interface config command.
It requires the switchport access vlan vlan-id interface config command.
questions.explanation: A routed port is created on a Layer 3 switch by disabling Layer 2 switchport behavior with the no switchport command. Routed ports can then be configured with an IPv4 address and do not support Layer 2 trunking or access VLAN assignment.

questions.question: What are two advantages of using a Layer 3 switch with SVIs for inter-VLAN routing?
options: It switches packets faster than using the router-on-a-stick method.
SVIs can be bundled into EtherChannels.
SVIs can be divided using subinterfaces.
SVIs eliminate the need for a default gateway in the hosts.
questions.explanation: Layer 3 switches provide inter-VLAN routing without requiring a separate router and use hardware-based switching for higher packet processing rates than router-on-a-stick.

questions.question: An EtherChannel link using LACP was formed between two switches, S1 and S2. While verifying the configuration, which mode combination could be utilized on both switches?
questions.explanation: An EtherChannel link using LACP forms when both sides are active, or when one side is active and the other is passive. Passive/passive will not initiate negotiation, and on mode does not use LACP.

questions.question: When a range of ports is being configured for EtherChannel, which mode will configure PAgP so that it initiates the EtherChannel negotiation?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode desirable command enables PAgP unconditionally and initiates negotiation. Auto waits to receive PAgP packets. Active and passive are LACP modes.

questions.question: Which three interface parameters must match for an EtherChannel to form?
questions.explanation: For EtherChannel, trunking mode, native VLAN, and allowed VLANs must match. Some negotiation modes can be different and still form a channel, such as active/passive or desirable/auto.

questions.question: What are three advantages of using EtherChannel technology?
options: Configuration tasks can be done on the EtherChannel interface.
A spanning tree recalculation is not required when a single link within the channel goes down.
The Spanning Tree Protocol shuts down the unused interfaces in the bundle to avoid loops.
There is no need to upgrade links to faster connections to increase bandwidth.
EtherChannel uses multiple logical links to provide redundancy.
Load balancing is not needed with EtherChannel.
questions.explanation: Configuration can be applied to the EtherChannel interface, existing ports can be bundled to increase bandwidth, and STP does not recalculate if only one member link fails. EtherChannel is one logical link and supports load balancing.

questions.question: A network administrator is configuring an EtherChannel link between two physical ports on a switch. Which statement describes the result when one of the physical ports fails?
options: The EtherChannel stops transmitting data until it is restarted.
The EtherChannel continues transmitting data with reduced bandwidth.
questions.explanation: EtherChannel is seen as one logical connection. If one member link fails, the channel remains functional but has reduced bandwidth, and STP recalculation is not required.

questions.question: When EtherChannel is implemented, multiple physical interfaces are bundled into which type of logical connection?
questions.explanation: EtherChannel bundles physical interfaces into a logical port-channel interface.

questions.question: When a range of ports is being configured for EtherChannel by the use of PAgP, which mode will form the bundled channel only if the port receives PAgP packets from another device?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode auto command enables PAgP only if the port receives a PAgP packet. Desirable actively initiates PAgP. Active and passive are LACP modes.

questions.question: Which two load balancing methods can be implemented with EtherChannel technology?
questions.explanation: Source MAC to destination MAC and source IP to destination IP are two load balancing methods used with EtherChannel.

questions.question: Which function is provided by EtherChannel?
options: enabling traffic from multiple VLANs to travel over a single Layer 2 link
spreading traffic across multiple physical WAN links
dividing the bandwidth of a single link into separate time slots
creating one logical link by using multiple physical links between two LAN switches
questions.explanation: EtherChannel groups several Fast Ethernet or Gigabit switch ports into one logical channel.

questions.question: Which statement is true about EtherChannel technology?
options: All configuration tasks must be done on the individual ports in the EtherChannel link.
STP does not run on redundant EtherChannel links.
Links must be upgraded to support EtherChannel.
questions.explanation: EtherChannel uses existing switch ports, so links do not have to be upgraded. STP still operates on EtherChannel, and configuration may be done on member ports or on the port-channel interface depending on the task.

questions.question: Which two mode combinations would result in the successful negotiation of an EtherChannel?
questions.explanation: Valid EtherChannel combinations include on/on, active/passive, active/active, desirable/auto, and desirable/desirable.

questions.question: Which two protocols are link aggregation protocols?
questions.explanation: PAgP and LACP, also known as IEEE 802.3ad, can be used to form EtherChannel. STP and RSTP prevent Layer 2 loops.

questions.question: When a range of ports is being configured for EtherChannel, which mode will configure LACP so that it initiates the EtherChannel negotiation?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode active command enables LACP unconditionally and initiates negotiation. Passive waits for LACP packets. Desirable and auto are PAgP modes.

questions.question: What will happen if a network administrator puts a port that is part of an EtherChannel bundle into a different VLAN than the other ports in that bundle?
options: The EtherChannel bundle will stay up if the ports were configured with no negotiation between the switches to form the EtherChannel.
The EtherChannel bundle will stay up if either PAgP or LACP is used.
The EtherChannel bundle will stay up only if LACP is used.
The EtherChannel bundle will stay up only if PAgP is used.
questions.explanation: All ports in an EtherChannel bundle must either be trunk ports or be access ports in the same VLAN. If VLAN settings do not match, the EtherChannel fails.

questions.question: When a range of ports is being configured for EtherChannel, which mode will configure LACP on a port only if the port receives LACP packets from another device?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode passive command enables LACP only if the port receives an LACP packet from another device.

questions.question: There has been an increase in network traffic between two Catalyst 2960 switches, and their FastEthernet trunk link has reached its capacity. How can traffic flow be improved?
options: Add routers between the switches to create additional broadcast domains.
Configure smaller VLANs to decrease the size of the collision domain.
Increase the speed of the ports using the bandwidth command.
questions.explanation: Bundling physical ports with EtherChannel increases available bandwidth between switches. Adding VLANs or routers does not solve trunk congestion, and the bandwidth command does not increase physical port speed.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the use of PAgP to create EtherChannels?
options: It increases the number of ports that are participating in spanning tree.
It mandates that an even number of ports (2, 4, 6, etc.) be used for aggregation.
It requires more physical links than LACP does
questions.explanation: PAgP is Cisco proprietary and automatically aggregates ports into an EtherChannel between Cisco devices. LACP can be used with Cisco and non-Cisco devices.

questions.question: Which combination of channel-group modes will establish an EtherChannel?
options: Switch 1 set to auto; switch 2 set to auto.
Switch 1 set to auto; switch 2 set to on.
Switch 1 set to desirable; switch 2 set to desirable.
Switch 1 set to on; switch 2 set to desirable.
questions.explanation: Desirable/desirable forms an EtherChannel because both sides actively negotiate. On mode does not negotiate, and auto/auto does not initiate negotiation.

questions.question: Which interface configuration command will enable the port to initiate an LACP EtherChannel?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode active command enables LACP unconditionally and initiates negotiation. Passive waits for LACP packets.

questions.question: Which interface configuration command will enable the port to establish an EtherChannel only if it receives PAgP packets from the other switch?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode auto command enables PAgP only if the port receives a PAgP packet from another device.

questions.question: Which statement describes a characteristic of EtherChannel?
options: It can combine up to a maximum of 4 physical links.
It can bundle mixed types of 100 Mbps and 1 Gbps Ethernet links.
It consists of multiple parallel links between a switch and a router.
It is made by combining multiple physical links that are seen as one link between two switches.
questions.explanation: EtherChannel combines multiple compatible Ethernet physical links so they are seen and configured as one logical link. Each EtherChannel can commonly include up to eight compatible Ethernet ports.

questions.question: What are two advantages of using LACP?
options: LACP allows automatic formation of EtherChannel links.
LACP allows use of multivendor devices.
LACP decreases the amount of configuration that is needed on a switch for EtherChannel.
LACP eliminates the need for the Spanning Tree Protocol.
LACP increases redundancy to Layer 3 devices.
LACP provides a simulated environment for testing link aggregation.
questions.explanation: LACP is part of IEEE 802.3ad and allows automatic EtherChannel negotiation by sending LACP packets. Because it is standards-based, it can be used in multivendor environments.

questions.question: Which three settings must match in order for switch ports to form an EtherChannel?
options: Non-trunk ports must belong to the same VLAN.
Port security violation settings on interconnecting ports must match.
The duplex settings on interconnecting ports must match.
The port channel group number on interconnecting switches must match.
The SNMP community strings must match.
The speed settings on interconnecting ports must match.
questions.explanation: All interfaces in an EtherChannel must have matching speed and duplex settings. If they are not trunks, they must belong to the same VLAN. SNMP strings and port security settings are not relevant to EtherChannel formation.

questions.question: Which statement is true about broadcast and collision domains?
options: The size of the collision domain can be reduced by adding hubs to a network.
Adding a switch to a network will increase the size of the broadcast domain.
Adding a router to a network will increase the size of the collision domain.
The more interfaces a router has the larger the resulting broadcast domain.
questions.explanation: A switch forwards broadcast frames out all other interfaces, including interfaces connected to other switches. Adding more switches can increase the size of the broadcast domain.

questions.question: What is one function of a Layer 2 switch?
options: forwards data based on logical addressing
determines which interface is used to forward a frame based on the destination MAC address
duplicates the electrical signal of each frame to every port
learns the port assigned to a host by examining the destination MAC address
questions.explanation: A Layer 2 switch uses the destination MAC address to look up the associated port in the MAC address table and forwards the frame to that port. It learns MAC addresses by examining source MAC addresses in inbound frames.

questions.question: What is the significant difference between a hub and a Layer 2 LAN switch?
options: A hub divides collision domains, and a switch divides broadcast domains.
Each port of a hub is a collision domain, and each port of a switch is a broadcast domain.
A switch creates many smaller collision domains, and a hub increases the size of a single collision domain.
A hub forwards frames, and a switch forwards only packets.
questions.explanation: Hubs operate at the physical layer and extend a single collision domain. Switches forward frames at Layer 2, and each switch port is a separate collision domain.

questions.question: What will a Cisco LAN switch do if it receives an incoming frame and the destination MAC address is not listed in the MAC address table?
options: Send the frame to the default gateway address.
Use ARP to resolve the port that is related to the frame.
Forward the frame out all ports except the port where the frame is received.
questions.explanation: When the destination MAC address is unknown, a switch floods the frame out all ports except the ingress port. When the destination device replies, the switch learns its source MAC address and port.

questions.question: Which switch characteristic helps alleviate network congestion when a 10 Gbps port is forwarding data to a 1 Gbps port?
questions.explanation: Frame buffers store ingress traffic until the slower egress port can transmit it. This helps reduce dropped frames and alleviate congestion.

questions.question: Which switching method makes use of the FCS value?
questions.explanation: Store-and-forward switching receives the entire frame and checks the frame-check sequence (FCS) before forwarding.

questions.question: What does the term “port density” represent for an Ethernet switch?
options: the memory space that is allocated to each switch port
the numbers of hosts that are connected to each switch port
questions.explanation: Port density is the number of ports available on a switch.

questions.question: Which information does a switch use to keep the MAC address table information current?
options: the source MAC address and the incoming port
the source and destination MAC addresses and the incoming port
the source and destination MAC addresses and the outgoing port
the destination MAC address and the incoming port
the source MAC address and the outgoing port
the destination MAC address and the outgoing port
questions.explanation: A switch maintains its MAC address table by using the source MAC address of incoming frames and the port on which those frames arrive.

questions.question: Which two statements are true about half-duplex and full-duplex communications?
options: Half duplex has only one channel.
Full duplex increases the effective bandwidth.
Full duplex allows both ends to transmit and receive simultaneously.
Full duplex offers 100 percent potential use of the bandwidth.
All modern NICS support both half-duplex and full-duplex communication.
questions.explanation: Full-duplex communication allows both ends to transmit and receive simultaneously, increasing effective bandwidth. Gigabit Ethernet and 10 Gb/s NICs require full duplex and do not support half-duplex operation.

questions.question: Which type of address does a switch use to build the MAC address table?
questions.explanation: A switch builds the MAC address table from the source MAC address in received frames and associates that address with the ingress port.

questions.question: Which option correctly describes a switching method?
options: cut-through: makes a forwarding decision after receiving the entire frame
cut-through: provides the flexibility to support any mix of Ethernet speeds
store-and-forward: forwards the frame immediately after examining its destination MAC address
store-and-forward: ensures that the frame is free of physical and data-link errors
questions.explanation: Store-and-forward switching receives the entire frame and performs error checking before forwarding. Cut-through switching begins forwarding after reading the destination MAC address.

questions.question: Which network device can serve as a boundary to divide a Layer 2 broadcast domain?
questions.explanation: Only a Layer 3 device, such as a router, can divide a Layer 2 broadcast domain.

questions.question: What is the purpose of frame buffers on a switch?
options: They execute checksum values before transmission.
They provide temporary storage of the frame checksum.
They hold traffic, thus alleviating network congestion.
They provide a basic security scan on received frames.
questions.explanation: Frame buffers store traffic waiting to be transmitted, which helps prevent drops when traffic arrives faster than it can leave.

questions.question: Which network device can be used to eliminate collisions on an Ethernet network?
questions.explanation: A switch provides microsegmentation. Each switch port is its own collision domain, eliminating collisions between devices on different switch ports.

questions.question: What criteria is used by a Cisco LAN switch to decide how to forward Ethernet frames?
questions.explanation: Cisco LAN switches use the destination MAC address and the MAC address table to make Ethernet frame forwarding decisions.

questions.question: What are two reasons a network administrator would segment a network with a Layer 2 switch?
options: To isolate ARP request messages from the rest of the network
questions.explanation: Layer 2 switching creates microsegmented connections that can give devices full-bandwidth, full-duplex connectivity during transmission and can isolate traffic between segments. Layer 2 switches do not isolate broadcasts such as ARP requests.

questions.question: A switch has received a frame on an ingress port. What will the switch do if the unicast destination MAC address is in the MAC address table?
options: It will forward the frame out all ports.
It will forward the frame out all ports except the incoming port.
It will forward the frame out of the specified port in the MAC address table.
questions.explanation: If the destination MAC address is in the MAC address table, the switch forwards the frame out of the specified port.

questions.question: A switch has received a frame on an ingress port. What will the switch do if the unicast destination MAC address is not in the MAC address table?
options: It will forward the frame out all ports.
It will forward the frame out all ports except the incoming port.
It will forward the frame out of the specified port in the MAC address table.
questions.explanation: If the unicast destination MAC address is unknown, the switch floods the frame out all ports except the incoming port. This is called unknown unicast flooding.

questions.question: A switch has received a frame on an ingress port. What will the switch do if the destination MAC address is a broadcast address?
options: It will forward the frame out all ports.
It will forward the frame out all ports except the incoming port.
It will forward the frame out of the specified port in the MAC address table.
questions.explanation: If the destination MAC address is broadcast or multicast, the switch floods the frame out all ports except the incoming port.

questions.question: Which switching method forwards the frame immediately after examining the destination MAC address?
questions.explanation: Cut-through switching can make a forwarding decision as soon as it reads and looks up the destination MAC address in the MAC address table.

questions.question: Which statement about half-duplex and full-duplex communication is true?
options: Gigabit Ethernet and 10 Gb/s NICs can operate in full-duplex or half-duplex.
Half-duplex communication allows both ends to transmit and receive simultaneously.
Half-duplex communication is unidirectional, or one direction at a time.
questions.explanation: Full-duplex communication allows simultaneous sending and receiving. Half-duplex communication is one direction at a time. Gigabit Ethernet and 10 Gb/s NICs require full duplex and do not support half-duplex operation.

questions.question: Which port state will switch ports immediately transition to when configured for PortFast?
questions.explanation: PortFast allows a switch port to bypass the listening and learning states and transition immediately to the forwarding state.

questions.question: After the election of the root bridge has been completed, how will switches find the best paths to the root bridge?
options: Each switch will analyze the port states of all neighbors and use the designated ports to forward traffic to the root.
Each switch will analyze the sum of all port costs to reach the root and use the path with the lowest cost.
Each switch will analyze the sum of the hops to reach the root and use the path with the fewest hops.
Each switch will analyze the BID of all neighbors to reach the root and use the path through the lowest BID neighbors.
questions.explanation: After the root bridge is elected, each switch determines the best path to the root bridge by summing the individual port costs along each path. The path with the lowest total cost is selected.

questions.question: Which is the default STP operation mode on Cisco Catalyst switches?
questions.explanation: Cisco switches running IOS 15.0 or later run PVST+ by default. Cisco Catalyst switches support PVST+, Rapid PVST+, and MSTP, but only one mode can be active at a time.

questions.question: What value determines the root bridge when all switches connected by trunk links have default STP configurations?
questions.explanation: When all switches use the same default bridge priority, the MAC address becomes the deciding factor in the root bridge election. For a given VLAN, the extended system ID is also the same across the switches.

questions.question: During the implementation of Spanning Tree Protocol, all switches are rebooted by the network administrator. What is the first step of the spanning-tree election process?
options: All the switches send out BPDUs advertising themselves as the root bridge.
Each switch determines the best path to forward traffic.
Each switch determines what port to block to prevent a loop from occurring.
Each switch with a lower root ID than its neighbor will not send BPDUs.
questions.explanation: After a Cisco switch boots, it sends BPDUs containing its own BID and initially advertises itself as the root bridge. After the root bridge is elected, paths and port states are selected.

questions.question: Which two concepts relate to a switch port that is intended to have only end devices attached and intended never to be used to connect to another switch? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The RSTP edge port concept corresponds to the Cisco PVST+ PortFast feature. An edge port connects to an end station and should immediately transition to forwarding.

questions.question: Which three port states are used by Rapid PVST+? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Rapid PVST+ uses the discarding, learning, and forwarding port states.

questions.question: When PVST is running over a switched network, which port state can participate in BPDU frame forwarding based on BPDUs received, but does not forward data frames?
questions.explanation: Ports in the listening state can participate in BPDU frame forwarding based on received BPDUs, but they do not forward data frames.

questions.question: Which STP port role is adopted by a switch port if there is no other port with a lower cost to the root bridge?
questions.explanation: The root port is the port on a non-root switch with the lowest path cost to reach the root bridge.

questions.question: Which two statements describe a switch port that is configured with PortFast? (Choose two.)
options: The switch port immediately transitions from the listening to the forwarding state.
The switch port immediately transitions from blocking to the forwarding state.
The switch port sends DHCP requests before transitioning to the forwarding state.
The switch port immediately processes any BPDUs before transitioning to the forwarding state.
The switch port should never receive BPDUs.
questions.explanation: A PortFast port immediately transitions from blocking to forwarding. PortFast should only be configured on ports connected to end devices, so the port should never receive BPDUs.

questions.question: What is one way to correct a spanning tree failure?
options: Replace the cables on failed STP links.
Manually remove redundant links in the switched network.
Insert redundant links to replace the failed STP links.
Replace all instances of STP with RSTP.
questions.explanation: When a spanning tree failure creates Layer 2 loops, removing redundant links in the failed segment can normalize traffic and CPU load while the STP issue is investigated.

questions.question: What additional information is contained in the 12-bit extended system ID of a BPDU?
questions.explanation: The extended system ID is a 12-bit field in the bridge ID that identifies the VLAN ID.

questions.question: An administrator is troubleshooting a switch and wants to verify if it is a root bridge. What command can be used to do this?
questions.explanation: The show spanning-tree command displays STP information, including root bridge details.

questions.question: What is an accurate description of redundancy?
options: designing a network to use multiple virtual devices to ensure that all traffic uses the best path through the internetwork
configuring a router with a complete MAC address database to ensure that all frames can be forwarded to the correct destination
designing a network to use multiple paths between switches to ensure there is no single point of failure
configuring a switch with proper security to ensure that all traffic forwarded through an interface is filtered
questions.explanation: Redundancy removes single points of failure by using multiple physical paths between switches in the network.

questions.question: Which three components are combined to form a bridge ID? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The bridge ID consists of the bridge priority, extended system ID, and MAC address.

questions.question: What is an advantage of PVST+?
options: PVST+ optimizes performance on the network through automatic selection of the root bridge.
PVST+ optimizes performance on the network through load sharing using multiple root bridges.
PVST+ reduces bandwidth consumption compared to traditional implementations of STP that use CST.
PVST+ requires fewer CPU cycles for all the switches in the network.
questions.explanation: PVST+ can optimize load sharing by allowing different VLANs to use different root bridges. This requires manual configuration; root bridges are not automatically selected for load sharing.

questions.question: In which two port states does a switch learn MAC addresses and process BPDUs in a PVST network? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Switches learn MAC addresses in the learning and forwarding states. They process BPDUs in the blocking, listening, learning, and forwarding states.

questions.question: What two features does Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) provide to ensure proper network operations? (Choose two.)
options: Link-state dynamic routing that provides redundant routes
Removing single points of failure with multiple Layer 2 switches
questions.explanation: STP supports correct operation when a network has multiple interconnected Layer 2 switches and redundant links that remove single points of failure.

questions.question: Which PVST+ feature ensures that configured switch edge ports do not cause Layer 2 loops if a port is mistakenly connected to another switch?
questions.explanation: BPDU guard places an edge port into an error-disabled state if the port receives a BPDU. This helps prevent Layer 2 loops when a PortFast edge port is connected incorrectly.

questions.question: What is an advantage of using STP in a LAN?
options: It combines multiple switch trunk links into a logical port channel link to increase bandwidth.
It decreases the size of the failure domain.
It provides firewall services to protect the LAN.
It temporarily disables redundant paths to stop Layer 2 loops.
questions.explanation: STP allows redundant physical connections between Layer 2 devices without creating Layer 2 loops by temporarily disabling ports that could create a loop.

questions.question: Which two statements regarding a PortFast enabled switch port are true? (Choose two.)
options: The port immediately transitions from blocking to forwarding state.
The port immediately transitions from listening to forwarding state.
The port immediately processes any BPDUs before transitioning to the forwarding state.
The port sends DHCP requests before transitioning to the forwarding state.
The port should never receive BPDUs.
questions.explanation: PortFast-enabled ports immediately transition from blocking to forwarding and should only be used on access ports connected to end devices. Such ports should never receive BPDUs.

questions.question: What happens to runt frames received by a Cisco Ethernet switch?
options: The frame is returned to the originating network device.
The frame is broadcast to all other devices on the same network.
The frame is sent to the default gateway.
questions.explanation: Ethernet devices drop runt frames, which are frames smaller than 64 bytes, to avoid forwarding unusable traffic.

questions.question: What are the two sizes (minimum and maximum) of an Ethernet frame? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The standard Ethernet frame size ranges from a minimum of 64 bytes to a maximum of 1518 bytes.

questions.question: What statement describes Ethernet?
options: It defines the most common LAN type in the world.
It is the required Layer 1 and 2 standard for Internet communication.
It defines a standard model used to describe how networking works.
It connects multiple sites such as routers located in different countries.
questions.explanation: Ethernet is the most common LAN technology. It works at OSI Layers 1 and 2.

questions.question: Which two statements describe features or functions of the logical link control sublayer in Ethernet standards? (Choose two.)
options: Logical link control is implemented in software.
Logical link control is specified in the IEEE 802.3 standard.
The LLC sublayer adds a header and a trailer to the data.
The data link layer uses LLC to communicate with the upper layers of the protocol suite.
The LLC sublayer is responsible for the placement and retrieval of frames on and off the media.
questions.explanation: LLC is implemented in software and provides the interface from the data link layer to upper-layer protocols. MAC handles media access and framing.

questions.question: What statement describes a characteristic of MAC addresses?
options: They are only routable within the private network.
They are added as part of a Layer 3 PDU.
questions.explanation: MAC addresses are designed to be globally unique. The OUI identifies the vendor, and the remaining bits identify the interface.

questions.question: Which statement is true about MAC addresses?
options: MAC addresses are implemented by software.
A NIC only needs a MAC address if connected to a WAN.
The first three bytes are used by the vendor assigned OUI.
The ISO is responsible for MAC addresses regulations.
questions.explanation: A MAC address is 48 bits. The first 24 bits, or first three bytes, are the vendor OUI assigned through IEEE.

questions.question: Which destination address is used in an ARP request frame?
questions.explanation: ARP requests are Layer 2 broadcasts, so the Ethernet destination MAC address is FFFF.FFFF.FFFF.

questions.question: What addressing information is recorded by a switch to build its MAC address table?
options: the destination Layer 3 address of incoming packets
the destination Layer 2 address of outgoing frames
the source Layer 3 address of outgoing packets
the source Layer 2 address of incoming frames
questions.explanation: A switch learns MAC addresses from the source MAC address of incoming frames and associates each address with the ingress port.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. The exhibit shows a small switched network and the contents of the MAC address table of the switch. PC1 has sent a frame addressed to PC3. What will the switch do with the frame?
questions.imageAlt: Small switched network with MAC address table. PC1 sends a frame to PC3.
options: The switch will discard the frame.
The switch will forward the frame only to port 2.
The switch will forward the frame to all ports except port 4.
The switch will forward the frame to all ports.
The switch will forward the frame only to ports 1 and 3.
questions.explanation: PC3 is not in the MAC address table, so the switch floods the unknown unicast frame out every port except the incoming port, port 4.

questions.question: Which switching method uses the CRC value in a frame?
questions.explanation: Store-and-forward switching receives the whole frame and checks the CRC/FCS before forwarding.

questions.question: What is auto-MDIX?
options: a type of port on a Cisco switch
a feature that detects Ethernet cable type
questions.explanation: Auto-MDIX lets a switch detect the cable type and adjust transmit/receive pairs automatically.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. PC1 issues an ARP request because it needs to send a packet to PC2. In this scenario, what will happen next?
questions.imageAlt: PC1 and PC2 are on the same local network connected to SW1.
options: PC2 will send an ARP reply with its MAC address.
RT1 will send an ARP reply with its Fa0/0 MAC address.
RT1 will send an ARP reply with the PC2 MAC address.
SW1 will send an ARP reply with the PC2 MAC address.
SW1 will send an ARP reply with its Fa0/1 MAC address.
questions.explanation: PC2 is on the same LAN and owns the requested IPv4 address, so PC2 replies with its MAC address.

questions.question: What is the aim of an ARP spoofing attack?
options: to associate IP addresses to the wrong MAC address
to overwhelm network hosts with ARP requests
to flood the network with ARP reply broadcasts
to fill switch MAC address tables with bogus addresses
questions.explanation: ARP spoofing poisons IP-to-MAC mappings so traffic is sent to the attacker or another wrong destination.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of port-based memory buffering?
options: Frames in the memory buffer are dynamically linked to destination ports.
All frames are stored in a common memory buffer.
Frames are buffered in queues linked to specific ports.
All ports on a switch share a single memory buffer.
questions.explanation: Port-based buffering stores frames in queues associated with specific ingress and egress ports.

questions.question: What is the minimum Ethernet frame size that will not be discarded by the receiver as a runt frame?
questions.explanation: Frames smaller than 64 bytes are runt frames and are discarded.

questions.question: What are two potential network problems that can result from ARP operation? (Choose two.)
options: Manually configuring static ARP associations could facilitate ARP poisoning or MAC address spoofing.
On large networks with low bandwidth, multiple ARP broadcasts could cause data communication delays.
Network attackers could manipulate MAC address and IP address mappings in ARP messages with the intent of intercepting network traffic.
Large numbers of ARP request broadcasts could cause the host MAC address table to overflow and prevent the host from communicating on the network.
Multiple ARP replies result in the switch MAC address table containing entries that match the MAC addresses of hosts that are connected to the relevant switch port.
questions.explanation: ARP broadcasts can create delays on large low-bandwidth networks, and attackers can manipulate ARP mappings to intercept traffic.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. A collision fragment, also known as a ____ frame, is a frame of fewer than 64 bytes in length.
questions.explanation: A runt frame is shorter than the minimum Ethernet frame size of 64 bytes.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. On a Cisco switch, ____ memory buffering is used to buffer frames in queues linked to specific incoming and outgoing ports.
questions.explanation: Port-based memory buffering uses queues linked to specific switch ports.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. ARP ____ is a technique that is used to send fake ARP messages to other hosts in the LAN.
questions.explanation: ARP spoofing, also called ARP poisoning, associates IP addresses with wrong MAC addresses.

questions.question: Which statement describes the treatment of ARP requests on the local link?
options: They must be forwarded by all routers on the local network.
They are received and processed by every device on the local network.
They are dropped by all switches on the local network.
They are received and processed only by the target device.
questions.explanation: ARP requests are local Layer 2 broadcasts. Every local device receives and processes them, but routers do not forward them.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. The switches are in their default configuration. Host A needs to communicate with host D, but host A does not have the MAC address for its default gateway. Which network hosts will receive the ARP request sent by host A?
questions.imageAlt: Host A, B, C and router R1 are on one local network; host D is beyond another router.
options: only hosts A, B, and C
only hosts A, B, C, and D
only hosts B, C, and router R1
questions.explanation: Host A broadcasts for the default gateway MAC address on the local LAN. Hosts B, C, and router R1 receive it; the router does not forward it to host D.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A switch with a default configuration connects four hosts. The ARP table for host A is shown. What happens when host A wants to send an IP packet to host D?
questions.imageAlt: Four hosts connected to one switch and host A ARP table with entries for B and C only.
options: Host A sends an ARP request to the MAC address of host D.
Host D sends an ARP request to host A.
Host A sends out the packet to the switch. The switch sends the packet only to the host D, which in turn responds.
Host A sends out a broadcast of FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF. Every other host connected to the switch receives the broadcast and host D responds with its MAC address.
questions.explanation: Host D is not in host A ARP table, so host A sends a Layer 2 broadcast. All other hosts on the LAN receive it, and host D replies.

questions.question: True or False? When a device is sending data to another device on a remote network, the Ethernet frame is sent to the MAC address of the default gateway.
questions.explanation: For a remote destination, the Ethernet frame is addressed to the local default gateway MAC address.

questions.question: The ARP table in a switch maps which two types of address together?
options: Layer 3 address to a Layer 2 address
Layer 3 address to a Layer 4 address
Layer 4 address to a Layer 2 address
Layer 2 address to a Layer 4 address
questions.explanation: ARP maps IPv4 Layer 3 addresses to MAC Layer 2 addresses.

questions.question: Match the characteristic to the forwarding method. (Not all options are used.)
questions.imageAlt: Matching activity for cut-through and store-and-forward switching characteristics.

pairs.left: checks the frame length before forwarding
begins forwarding when the destination address is received

questions.explanation: Store-and-forward receives and validates the full frame. Cut-through begins forwarding earlier, reducing latency but possibly forwarding bad or runt frames.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of a contention-based access method?
options: It processes more overhead than the controlled access methods do.
It has mechanisms to track the turns to access the media.
It scales very well under heavy media use.
questions.explanation: Contention-based access is nondeterministic because devices compete for access to the medium.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the preamble in an Ethernet frame?
options: is used as a padding for data
is used to identify the source address
is used to identify the destination address
questions.explanation: The preamble provides timing synchronization so the receiver can lock onto the incoming frame.

questions.question: What is the Layer 2 multicast MAC address that corresponds to the Layer 3 IPv4 multicast address 224.139.34.56?
questions.explanation: IPv4 multicast MAC addresses begin with 01-00-5E and use the lower 23 bits of the multicast IPv4 address.

questions.question: Which two statements are correct about MAC and IP addresses during data transmission if NAT is not involved? (Choose two.)
options: A packet that has crossed four routers has changed the destination IP address four times.
Destination MAC addresses will never change in a frame that goes across seven routers.
Destination and source MAC addresses have local significance and change every time a frame goes from one LAN to another.
Destination IP addresses in a packet header remain constant along the entire path to a target host.
Every time a frame is encapsulated with a new destination MAC address, a new destination IP address is needed.
questions.explanation: Without NAT, IP source and destination addresses remain end-to-end. MAC addresses are rewritten at each Layer 3 hop for the next local link.

questions.question: What are two features of ARP? (Choose two.)
options: If a host is ready to send a packet to a local destination device and it has the IP address but not the MAC address of the destination, it generates an ARP broadcast.
An ARP request is sent to all devices on the Ethernet LAN and contains the IP address of the destination host and its multicast MAC address.
When a host is encapsulating a packet into a frame, it refers to the MAC address table to determine the mapping of IP addresses to MAC addresses.
If no device responds to the ARP request, then the originating node will broadcast the data packet to all devices on the network segment.
If a device receiving an ARP request has the destination IPv4 address, it responds with an ARP reply.
questions.explanation: ARP broadcasts a request when a local IPv4-to-MAC mapping is missing, and the host with the target IPv4 address replies.

questions.question: A host is trying to send a packet to a device on a remote LAN segment, but there are currently no mappings in its ARP cache. How will the device obtain a destination MAC address?
options: It will send an ARP request for the MAC address of the destination device.
It will send an ARP request for the MAC address of the default gateway.
It will send the frame and use its own MAC address as the destination.
It will send the frame with a broadcast MAC address.
It will send a request to the DNS server for the destination MAC address.
questions.explanation: For a remote network, the host needs the MAC address of its default gateway, not the final remote host.

questions.question: A network administrator is connecting two modern switches using a straight-through cable. The switches are new and have never been configured. Which three statements are correct about the final result of the connection? (Choose three.)
options: The link between the switches will work at the fastest speed that is supported by both switches.
The link between switches will work as full-duplex.
If both switches support different speeds, they will each work at their own fastest speed.
The auto-MDIX feature will configure the interfaces eliminating the need for a crossover cable.
The connection will not be possible unless the administrator changes the cable to a crossover cable.
The duplex capability has to be manually configured because it cannot be negotiated.
questions.explanation: Modern switches negotiate common speed/duplex settings and auto-MDIX handles straight-through or crossover cable pairing.

questions.question: A Layer 2 switch is used to switch incoming frames from a 1000BASE-T port to a port connected to a 100Base-T network. Which method of memory buffering would work best for this task?
questions.explanation: Shared memory buffering is useful when frames move between ports of different speeds because buffer memory is dynamically allocated.

questions.question: When would a switch record multiple entries for a single switch port in its MAC address table?
options: when a router is connected to the switch port
when multiple ARP broadcasts have been forwarded
when another switch is connected to the switch port
when the switch is configured for Layer 3 switching
questions.explanation: If another switch is connected to a port, multiple devices behind that switch can be learned on the same local port.

questions.question: Which two statements describe a fixed configuration Ethernet switch? (Choose two.)
options: The switch cannot be configured with multiple VLANs.
An SVI cannot be configured on the switch.
A fixed configuration switch may be stackable.
The number of ports on the switch cannot be increased.
The port density of the switch is determined by the Cisco IOS.
questions.explanation: A fixed configuration switch has a fixed number of ports, though some models can be stacked.

questions.question: How does adding an Ethernet line card affect the form factor of a switch?
options: by increasing the back plane switching speed
questions.explanation: A line card adds physical interfaces, increasing port density on a modular switch.

questions.question: Which address or combination of addresses does a Layer 3 switch use to make forwarding decisions?
questions.explanation: A Layer 3 switch can use IP information for routing and MAC information for local frame forwarding.

questions.question: What statement illustrates a drawback of the CSMA/CD access method?
options: Deterministic media access protocols slow network performance.
It is more complex than non-deterministic protocols.
CSMA/CD LAN technologies are only available at slower speeds than other LAN technologies.
questions.explanation: CSMA/CD allows collisions on shared half-duplex Ethernet media, and collisions reduce performance.

questions.question: Open the PT activity shown in the exhibit. What destination address will PC1 include in the destination address field of the Ethernet frame that it sends to PC2?
questions.imageAlt: Packet Tracer activity showing PC1 ARP cache after pinging PC2.
questions.explanation: PC1 sends the Ethernet frame to PC2 MAC address learned in ARP cache: 0030.a3e5.0401.

questions.question: Which address or combination of addresses does a Layer 3 switch use to make forwarding decisions?
questions.explanation: Layer 3 switches use both IP addresses for routing decisions and MAC addresses for Layer 2 forwarding.

questions.question: A network administrator issues the following commands on a Layer 3 switch: DLS1(config)# interface f0/3; DLS1(config-if)# no switchport; DLS1(config-if)# ip address 172.16.0.1 255.255.255.0; DLS1(config-if)# no shutdown. What is the administrator configuring?
questions.imageAlt: Layer 3 switch commands: interface f0/3, no switchport, IP address, no shutdown.
questions.explanation: The no switchport command converts the physical switch interface into a routed Layer 3 port.

questions.question: Match the seven fields of an Ethernet frame to their respective contents. (Not all options are used.)
questions.imageAlt: Matching activity with Ethernet frame fields 1 through 7.
questions.explanation: Ethernet frame order is preamble, SFD, destination MAC, source MAC, length/type, data, and FCS.

questions.question: What destination MAC address would be included in a frame sent from a source device to a destination device on the same local network?
options: The MAC address of the local router interface.
A broadcast MAC address of FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF.
The MAC address of the destination device.
questions.explanation: For a destination on the same local network, the Ethernet frame uses the destination device MAC address.

questions.question: What destination MAC address would be included in a frame sent from a source device to a destination device on a remote network?
options: A broadcast MAC address of FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF.
The MAC address of the local router interface.
The MAC address of the destination device.
questions.explanation: For a remote destination, the source sends the frame to the local default gateway, so the destination MAC address is the local router interface MAC address.

questions.question: What two protocols are used to determine the MAC address of a known destination device IP address for IPv4 and IPv6? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: IPv4 uses ARP for address resolution. IPv6 uses Neighbor Discovery (ND).

questions.question: What two functions are provided by ARP? (Choose two.)
options: Resolves IPv6 addresses to MAC addresses
Maintains a table of IPv6 to MAC address mappings
Maintains a table of IPv4 to MAC address mappings
Maintains a table of IPv4 address to domain names
Resolves IPv4 addresses to domain names
Resolves IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses
questions.explanation: ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses and maintains an ARP table of IPv4-to-MAC mappings.

questions.question: Where is the ARP table stored on a device?
questions.explanation: The ARP table is cached in RAM.

questions.question: Which statement is true about ARP?
options: An ARP cache cannot be manually deleted.
questions.explanation: ARP entries are temporary cache entries and can age out or be cleared.

questions.question: Which command could be used on a Cisco router to view its ARP table?
questions.explanation: On Cisco IOS, show ip arp displays the ARP table.

questions.question: What is an attack using ARP?
questions.explanation: ARP poisoning uses forged ARP messages to corrupt IP-to-MAC mappings.

questions.question: Which two ICMPv6 messages are used in SLAAC? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: SLAAC uses Router Solicitation and Router Advertisement messages.

questions.question: Which two ICMPv6 messages are used to determine the MAC address of a known IPv6 address? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: IPv6 Neighbor Discovery resolves MAC addresses by using Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement messages.

questions.question: To what type of address are ICMPv6 neighbor solicitation messages sent?
questions.explanation: Neighbor Solicitation messages are sent to an IPv6 multicast address. IPv6 does not use broadcast.

questions.question: Which router component holds the routing table, ARP cache, and running configuration file?
questions.explanation: RAM stores active runtime data, including the routing table, ARP cache, and running configuration.

questions.question: What type of information is contained in an ARP table?
options: Domain name to IPv4 address mappings
IPv4 address to MAC address mappings
Switch ports associated with destination MAC addresses
questions.explanation: An ARP table contains IPv4 address to MAC address mappings.

questions.question: A PC is configured to obtain an IPv4 address automatically from network 192.168.1.0/24. The network administrator issues the arp -a command and notices an entry of 192.168.1.255 ff-ff-ff-ff-ff-ff. Which statement describes this entry?
options: This is a dynamic map entry.
This entry maps to the default gateway.
This is a static map entry.
This entry refers to the PC itself.
questions.explanation: 192.168.1.255 is the broadcast address for 192.168.1.0/24 and is statically mapped to FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF.

questions.question: A cybersecurity analyst believes an attacker is spoofing the MAC address of the default gateway to perform a man-in-the-middle attack. Which command should the analyst use to view the MAC address a host is using to reach the default gateway?
questions.explanation: On a Windows host, arp -a displays the ARP cache and the MAC address mapped to the default gateway IPv4 address.

questions.question: What will a Layer 2 switch do when the destination MAC address of a received frame is not in the MAC table?
options: It forwards the frame out of all ports except for the port at which the frame was received.
It broadcasts the frame out of all ports on the switch.
It notifies the sending host that the frame cannot be delivered.
questions.explanation: Unknown unicast frames are flooded out all switch ports except the ingress port.

questions.question: Which two ICMPv6 messages are used during the Ethernet MAC address resolution process? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement ICMPv6 messages for MAC address resolution.

questions.question: How does the ARP process use an IPv4 address?
options: To determine the network number based on the number of bits in the IPv4 address
To determine the amount of time a packet takes when traveling from source to destination
To determine the MAC address of the remote destination host
To determine the MAC address of a device on the same network
questions.explanation: ARP maps a known IPv4 address to the MAC address of a device reachable on the same local network. For remote networks, ARP resolves the default gateway MAC address.

questions.question: What is one function of the ARP protocol?
options: Resolving an IPv4 address to a MAC address
Maintaining a table of domain names with their resolved IP addresses
Mapping a domain name to its IP address
questions.explanation: ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses. DHCP obtains IP configuration, and DNS maps names to IP addresses.

questions.question: Which action is taken by a Layer 2 switch when it receives a Layer 2 broadcast frame?
options: It sends the frame to all ports.
It sends the frame to all ports except the port on which it received the frame.
It sends the frame to all ports that are registered to forward broadcasts.
questions.explanation: A Layer 2 switch floods broadcast frames out all ports except the port where the frame arrived.

questions.question: What addresses are mapped by ARP?
options: Destination IPv4 address to the source MAC address
Destination IPv4 address to the destination host name
Destination MAC address to the source IPv4 address
IPv4 address to a destination MAC address
questions.explanation: ARP maps an IPv4 address to the destination MAC address needed for Ethernet encapsulation.

questions.question: When an IPv4 packet is sent to a host on a remote network, what information is provided by ARP?
options: The IPv4 address of the default gateway
The IPv4 address of the destination host
The MAC address of the switch port that connects to the sending host
The MAC address of the router interface closest to the sending host
questions.explanation: For a remote destination, ARP discovers the MAC address of the default gateway router interface on the local network.

questions.question: The ARP table in a switch maps which two types of address together?
options: Layer 4 address to a Layer 2 address
Layer 3 address to a Layer 4 address
Layer 3 address to a Layer 2 address
Layer 2 address to a Layer 4 address
questions.explanation: The ARP table maps Layer 3 IPv4 addresses to Layer 2 MAC addresses.

questions.question: What is the purpose of ARP in an IPv4 network?
options: To forward data onward based on the destination IP address
To forward data onward based on the destination MAC address.
To obtain a specific MAC address when an IP address is known
To build the MAC address table in a switch from the information that is gathered
questions.explanation: ARP obtains a MAC address when the IPv4 address is known and stores the mapping in the ARP table.

questions.question: Which destination address is used in an ARP request frame?
questions.explanation: ARP requests use the Layer 2 broadcast destination MAC address FFFF.FFFF.FFFF.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model is concerned with end-to-end communication over the network?
questions.explanation: The network layer, or OSI Layer 3, provides services to allow end-to-end communication across a network.
questions.reference: User provided; based on CCNA 1 Chapter 6 Network Layer

questions.question: Which of the following is associated with the network layer?
questions.explanation: The network layer uses Layer 3 addressing such as IPv4 and IPv6 to identify end hosts.
questions.reference: User provided; based on CCNA 1 Chapter 6 Network Layer

questions.question: Why was IPv4 designed as a connectionless protocol?
options: IP is connectionless, which greatly reduces the overhead of IP. Therefore, there is no initial exchange of control information before packets are forwarded, and no additional fields exist in the header to maintain an established connection.
questions.explanation: IP is connectionless, which greatly reduces the overhead of IP. Therefore, there is no initial exchange of control information before packets are forwarded, and no additional fields exist in the header to maintain an established connection.
questions.reference: User provided; based on CCNA 1 Chapter 6 Network Layer

questions.question: On a router, what field in an IPv4 header should be examined to determine that the maximum number of hops have been reached by the packet on its way from the source to this destination?
questions.explanation: Time-to-Live (TTL) contains an 8-bit binary value that is used to limit the lifetime of a packet. It is specified in seconds but is commonly referred to as hop count.
questions.reference: User provided; based on CCNA 1 Chapter 6 Network Layer

questions.question: When configuring a host, the gateway was not configured. How will this affect communication to and from this device?
options: Host communication will not be affected.
The host will not be able to communicate with devices by name.
Communication will be limited to hosts in the local network.
No communication will be successful to or from the host.
questions.explanation: Without a proper default gateway, a host will not know where to send packets for communication to remote networks. Therefore, the host cannot communication outside its local network.
questions.reference: User provided; based on CCNA 1 Chapter 6 Network Layer

questions.question: In what part of a router is the current configuration being used located?
questions.explanation: The running configuration file is located in RAM and is the configuration file that stores the configuration commands that the router IOS is currently using. It is also known as the running config.
questions.reference: User provided; based on CCNA 1 Chapter 6 Network Layer

questions.question: During the boot process of a Cisco router, you notice a series of hash symbols (#) appearing on the terminal emulator screen from the console session. In what phase is the boot process?
questions.explanation: During self-decompression of the IOS image file, a string of hash (pound) signs will be displayed.
questions.reference: User provided; based on CCNA 1 Chapter 6 Network Layer

questions.question: What are the required steps for configuring an interface on a router? (Choose two.)
options: Add a description to the interface
Turn on routing on the interface
questions.explanation: The requirement for router interface configuration is to provide Layer 3 (IPv4, IPv6, and so on) addressing information and to enable the interface.
questions.reference: User provided; based on CCNA 1 Chapter 6 Network Layer

questions.question: The ip default-gateway command was not used when configuring a switch. How will this affect network communication? (Choose two.)
options: Host communication through the switch will not be affected.
The hosts communicating through the switch will not be able to communicate with devices by name.
The host communication through the switch will be limited to hosts in the local network.
No communication through the switch will be successful.
Communication to and from the switch will be limited to hosts in the local network.
questions.explanation: A common misconception is that the switch uses its configured default gateway address to determine where to forward packets originating from hosts connected to the switch and destined for hosts on a remote network. Actually, the IP address and default gateway information is only used for packets that originate from the switch.
questions.reference: User provided; based on CCNA 1 Chapter 6 Network Layer

questions.question: When using the netstat -r command on a host, you see a route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0.0. What does this route represent?
options: The host has no routes available for forwarding packets.
This is a route for testing local communication.
Destinations without a specified route are forwarded to the gateway.
The host does not have an IP address configured.
questions.explanation: The local default route (0.0.0.0), that is, all packets with destinations that do not match other specified addresses in the routing table, are forwarded to the gateway.
questions.reference: User provided; based on CCNA 1 Chapter 6 Network Layer

questions.question: Which command can be used on a Windows host to display the routing table?
questions.explanation: On a Windows host, either the route print or netstat -r commands can be used to display the host routing table. The show ip route command is used on a router to display its routing table. The netstat -s command is used to display per-protocol statistics. The tracert command is used to display the path that a packet travels to its destination.

questions.question: What information is added during encapsulation at OSI Layer 3?
questions.explanation: IP is a Layer 3 protocol. The Layer 3 header contains IP-related information including the source and destination IP addresses.

questions.question: How does the network layer use the MTU value?
options: The network layer depends on the higher level layers to determine the MTU.
The network layer depends on the data link layer to set the MTU, and adjusts the speed of transmission to accommodate it.
The MTU is passed to the network layer by the data link layer.
To increase speed of delivery, the network layer ignores the MTU.
questions.explanation: The data link layer indicates to the network layer the MTU for the medium that is being used. The network layer uses that information to determine how large the packet can be when it is forwarded.

questions.question: Which characteristic describes an IPv6 enhancement over IPv4?
options: IPv6 addresses are based on 128-bit flat addressing as opposed to IPv4 which is based on 32-bit hierarchical addressing.
The IPv6 header is simpler than the IPv4 header is, which improves packet handling.
Both IPv4 and IPv6 support authentication, but only IPv6 supports privacy capabilities.
The IPv6 address space is four times bigger than the IPv4 address space.
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses 128-bit hierarchical addressing and a simplified header with fewer fields, improving packet handling. The IPv6 address space is much larger than IPv4.

questions.question: When a connectionless protocol is in use at a lower layer of the OSI model, how is missing data detected and retransmitted if necessary?
options: Connectionless acknowledgements are used to request retransmission.
Upper-layer connection-oriented protocols keep track of the data received and can request retransmission from the upper-level protocols on the sending host.
Network layer IP protocols manage the communication sessions if connection-oriented transport services are not available.
The best-effort delivery process guarantees that all packets that are sent are received.
questions.explanation: When connectionless protocols are in use at lower layers, upper-level protocols may need to account for and retransmit lost data.

questions.question: What was the reason for the creation and implementation of IPv6?
options: to make reading a 32-bit address easier
to provide more address space in the Internet Names Registry
to allow NAT support for private addressing
questions.explanation: IPv6 was created to relieve IPv4 address depletion by expanding the address length from 32 bits to 128 bits.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes a characteristic of IPv4?
options: All IPv4 addresses are assignable to hosts.
An IPv4 header has fewer fields than an IPv6 header has.
questions.explanation: IPv4 has a 32-bit address space. Some addresses are reserved, IPv4 does not natively support IPsec, and IPv6 has a simpler header.

questions.question: Which field in an IPv4 packet header will typically stay the same during its transmission?
questions.explanation: The destination address field typically stays the same during transmission, while other fields can change.

questions.question: When a router receives a packet, what information must be examined in order for the packet to be forwarded to a remote destination?
questions.explanation: A router examines the destination IP address and uses the routing table to find the best path.

questions.question: Which field in an IPv6 packet is used by the router to determine if a packet has expired and should be dropped?
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses the Hop Limit field instead of the IPv4 TTL field.

questions.question: Which information is used by routers to forward a data packet toward its destination?
questions.explanation: Routers use the destination IP address to forward packets toward the destination.

questions.question: A computer has to send a packet to a destination host in the same LAN. How will the packet be sent?
options: The packet will be sent to the default gateway first, and then, depending on the response from the gateway, it may be sent to the destination host.
The packet will be sent directly to the destination host.
The packet will first be sent to the default gateway, and then from the default gateway it will be sent directly to the destination host.
The packet will be sent only to the default gateway.
questions.explanation: If the destination host is in the same LAN, the packet is sent directly to the destination host.

questions.question: A router receives a packet from the Gigabit 0/0 interface and determines that the packet needs to be forwarded out the Gigabit 0/1 interface. What will the router do next?
options: route the packet out the Gigabit 0/1 interface
create a new Layer 2 Ethernet frame to be sent to the destination
look into the ARP cache to determine the destination IP address
look into the routing table to determine if the destination network is in the routing table
questions.explanation: After deciding the outgoing interface, the router builds a new Layer 2 frame for the outgoing link and forwards it.

questions.question: Which IPv4 address can a host use to ping the loopback interface?
questions.explanation: A host can ping the loopback interface using an address in 127.0.0.0/8, commonly 127.0.0.1.

questions.question: Which characteristic of the network layer in the OSI model allows carrying packets for multiple types of communications among many hosts?
options: the de-encapsulation of headers from lower layers
the selection of paths for and direct packets toward the destination
the ability to operate without regard to the data that is carried in each packet
the ability to manage the data transport between processes running on hosts
questions.explanation: Network layer protocols define packet structure and processing. Operating without regard to the data carried in each packet allows the network layer to carry multiple communication types.

questions.question: What are two characteristics of IP? (Choose two.)
options: does not require a dedicated end-to-end connection
operates independently of the network media
re-assembles out of order packets into the correct order at the receiver end
questions.explanation: IP is connectionless, best-effort, and media independent.

questions.question: Which field in the IPv4 header is used to prevent a packet from traversing a network endlessly?
questions.explanation: The TTL field limits packet lifetime and is decremented by routers.

questions.question: What IPv4 header field identifies the upper layer protocol carried in the packet?
questions.explanation: The Protocol field identifies the upper-layer protocol carried in the packet.

questions.question: What is one advantage that the IPv6 simplified header offers over IPv4?
options: smaller-sized source and destination IP addresses
questions.explanation: The simplified IPv6 header supports more efficient packet handling.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Which route from the PC1 routing table will be used to reach PC2?
options: A. Network Destination 192.168.10.0, Netmask 255.255.255.0, Gateway On-link, Interface 192.168.10.10, Metric 281
B. Network Destination 192.168.10.10, Netmask 255.255.255.255, Gateway On-link, Interface 192.168.10.10, Metric 281

D. Network Destination 0.0.0.0, Netmask 0.0.0.0, Gateway 192.168.10.1, Interface 192.168.10.10, Metric 25
questions.explanation: PC1 and PC2 are both on 192.168.10.0/24, so the local network route is used.
