questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. R1 receives a packet destined for the IP address 192.168.2.10. Out which interface will R1 forward the packet?
questions.explanation: If a route points to a next-hop address, the router performs a second lookup to determine the outgoing interface.
questions.imageAlt: Refer to the exhibit. R1 receives a packet destined for the IP address 192.168.2.10. Out which interface will R1 forward the packet?

questions.question: What type of route is indicated by the code C in an IPv4 routing table on a Cisco router?
options: dynamic route that is learned through EIGRP
questions.explanation: In a Cisco routing table, C indicates a directly connected route.

questions.question: What routing table entry has a next hop address associated with a destination network?
questions.explanation: Remote route entries include a next-hop IP address.

questions.question: Which statement describes a hardware feature of a Cisco 1941 router that has the default hardware configuration?
options: It does not have an AUX port.
It has three FastEthernet interfaces for LAN access.
It has two types of ports that can be used to access the console.
It does not require a CPU because it relies on Compact Flash to run the IOS.
questions.explanation: A Cisco 1941 has RJ-45 and USB console access ports.

questions.question: Following default settings, what is the next step in the router boot sequence after the IOS loads from flash?
options: Locate and load the startup-config file from NVRAM.
Load the bootstrap program from ROM.
Load the running-config file from RAM.
questions.explanation: The router boot sequence performs POST, loads IOS, then loads the startup configuration from NVRAM.

questions.question: What are two types of router interfaces? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Router interfaces are commonly grouped as LAN interfaces and WAN interfaces.

questions.question: Which two pieces of information are in the RAM of a Cisco router during normal operation? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The IOS image is copied into RAM during boot, and the IP routing table is stored in RAM.

questions.question: A router boots and enters setup mode. What is the reason for this?
options: Cisco IOS is missing from flash memory.
The configuration file is missing from NVRAM.
The POST process has detected hardware failure.
questions.explanation: If the router cannot locate the startup-config file in NVRAM, it enters setup mode.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the startup configuration file on a Cisco router?
options: to facilitate the basic operation of the hardware components of a device
to contain the commands that are used to initially configure a router on startup
to contain the configuration commands that the router IOS is currently using
to provide a limited backup version of the IOS, in case the router cannot load the full featured IOS
questions.explanation: The startup configuration is stored in NVRAM and contains commands used to configure the router at startup.

questions.question: Which three commands are used to set up secure access to a router through a connection to the console interface? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Console password protection uses line console 0, password cisco, and login.

questions.question: Open the PT Activity. The enable password on all devices is cisco. Perform the tasks in the activity instructions and then answer the question. For what reason is the failure occurring?
options: PC1 has an incorrect default gateway configured.
SW1 does not have a default gateway configured.
The IP address of SW1 is configured in a wrong subnet.
PC2 has an incorrect default gateway configured.
questions.explanation: The ip default-gateway command is missing on SW1.

questions.question: Match the command with the device mode at which the command is entered. (Not all options are used.)
questions.explanation: Each command is available only in its matching IOS command mode.

questions.question: When connectionless protocols are implemented at the lower layers of the OSI model, what are usually used to acknowledge the data receipt and request the retransmission of missing data?
questions.explanation: Upper-layer connection-oriented protocols can acknowledge received data and request retransmission.

questions.question: Which IPv4 header field is responsible for defining the priority of the packet?
questions.explanation: The Differentiated Services field defines packet priority.

questions.question: Why is NAT not needed in IPv6?
options: Because IPv6 has integrated security, there is no need to hide the IPv6 addresses of internal networks.
Any host or user can get a public IPv6 network address because the number of available IPv6 addresses is extremely large.
The problems that are induced by NAT applications are solved because the IPv6 header improves packet handling by intermediate routers.
The end-to-end connectivity problems that are caused by NAT are solved because the number of routes increases with the number of nodes that are connected to the Internet.
questions.explanation: The large IPv6 address space reduces the need for NAT.

questions.question: What is a service provided by the Flow Label field of the IPv6 header?
options: It limits the lifetime of a packet.
It identifies the total length of the IPv6 packet.
It classifies packets for traffic congestion control.
It informs network devices to maintain the same path for real-time application packets.
questions.explanation: The Flow Label can help network devices keep the same path for real-time packet flows.

questions.question: How do hosts ensure that their packets are directed to the correct network destination?
options: They have to keep their own local routing table that contains a route to the loopback interface, a local network route, and a remote default route.
They always direct their packets to the default gateway, which will be responsible for the packet delivery.
They search in their own local routing table for a route to the network destination address and pass this information to the default gateway.
They send a query packet to the default gateway asking for the best route.
questions.explanation: Hosts maintain a local routing table with loopback, local network, and default routes.

questions.question: Which two commands can be used on a Windows host to display the routing table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Windows hosts can use route print or netstat -r to display the routing table.

questions.question: During the process of forwarding traffic, what will the router do immediately after matching the destination IP address to a network on a directly connected routing table entry?
options: discard the traffic after consulting the route table
look up the next-hop address for the packet
switch the packet to the directly connected interface
questions.explanation: When the destination is on a directly connected interface, the packet is switched to that interface.

questions.question: A technician is configuring a router that is actively running on the network. Suddenly, power to the router is lost. If the technician has not saved the configuration, which two types of information will be lost? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The routing table and ARP cache are in volatile memory and are lost when power is lost.

questions.question: Which two interfaces will allow access via the VTY lines to configure the router? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: VTY access is remote access over IP through LAN or WAN interfaces.

questions.question: Which two files, if found, are copied into RAM as a router with the default configuration register setting boots up? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The IOS image and startup configuration are copied into RAM during boot.

questions.question: When would the Cisco IOS image held in ROM be used to boot the router?
options: when the full IOS cannot be found
when the running configuration directs the router to do this
questions.explanation: The limited IOS in ROM is used when the full IOS cannot be found.

questions.question: After troubleshooting a router, the network administrator wants to save the router configuration so that it will be used automatically the next time that the router reboots. What command should be issued?
questions.explanation: copy running-config startup-config saves the current configuration to NVRAM for the next boot.

questions.question: Which three commands are used to set up a password for a person who attaches a cable to a new router so that an initial configuration can be performed? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Initial console access password configuration uses line console 0, password cisco, and login.

questions.question: Which statement about router interfaces is true?
options: Router LAN interfaces are not activated by default, but router WAN interfaces are.
Once the no shutdown command is given, a router interface is active and operational.
Commands that apply an IP address and subnet mask to an interface are entered in global configuration mode.
A configured and activated router interface must be connected to another device in order to operate.
questions.explanation: A router interface must be configured, enabled, and connected to another device to become operational.

questions.question: Which command displays a summary chart of all router interfaces, their IP addresses, and their current operational status?
questions.explanation: show ip interface brief displays a summary of interfaces, IP addresses, and status.

questions.question: A technician is manually configuring a computer with the necessary IP parameters to communicate over the corporate network. The computer already has an IP address, a subnet mask, and a DNS server. What else has to be configured for Internet access?
options: the domain name of the organization
questions.explanation: A default gateway is required to reach remote networks such as the Internet.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A packet leaving PC-1 has to traverse how many hops to reach PC-4?
questions.explanation: The packet crosses three routers, so it traverses 3 hops.
questions.imageAlt: Refer to the exhibit. A packet leaving PC-1 has to traverse how many hops to reach PC-4?

questions.question: Fill in the blank. In a router, which nonvolatile memory stores the diagnostic software, bootup instructions, and a limited IOS?
questions.explanation: ROM stores diagnostic software, bootup instructions, and a limited IOS.

questions.question: Open the PT Activity. Perform the tasks in the activity instructions and then answer the question or complete the task. Does the router have enough RAM and flash memory to support the new IOS?
options: The router has enough RAM and flash memory for the IOS upgrade.
The router has enough RAM, but needs more flash memory for the IOS upgrade.
The router has enough flash memory, but needs more RAM for the IOS upgrade.
The router needs more RAM and more flash memory for the IOS upgrade.
questions.explanation: The activity result indicates that both RAM and flash memory are sufficient for the IOS upgrade.

questions.question: Match the configuration mode with the command that is available in that mode. (Not all options are used.)
questions.explanation: Each command is entered from the IOS mode where it is available.

questions.question: Match field names to the IP header where they would be found. (Not all options are used.)
questions.explanation: Flags and Total Length are IPv4 fields; Traffic Class and Flow Label are IPv6 fields.

questions.question: Which type of static route that is configured on a router uses only the exit interface?
questions.explanation: A directly connected static route specifies only the exit interface.

questions.question: Match the packets with their destination IP address to the exiting interfaces on the router. (Not all targets are used.)
questions.explanation: Use the longest matching route in the routing table. Destinations in 172.17.10.0/24 exit FastEthernet1/1, destinations in 172.17.12.0/24 exit FastEthernet1/0, destinations in 172.17.14.0/24 exit FastEthernet0/1, destinations in 172.17.6.0/24 exit FastEthernet0/0, and destinations without a more specific route use the default route through Serial0/0/0.
questions.imageAlt: Match the packets with their destination IP address to the exiting interfaces on the router. (Not all targets are used.)

questions.question: How many bits are in an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: An IPv4 address is made of four 8-bit octets, for a total of 32 bits.

questions.question: Which two parts are components of an IPv4 address? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: An IPv4 address has a network portion and a host portion. The subnet mask identifies where the network portion ends and the host portion begins.

questions.question: What does the IP address 172.17.4.250/24 represent?
questions.explanation: With /24, the network is 172.17.4.0 and the broadcast address is 172.17.4.255, so 172.17.4.250 is a usable host address.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the subnet mask in conjunction with an IP address?
options: to uniquely identify a host on a network
to identify whether the address is public or private
to determine the subnet to which the host belongs
to mask the IP address to outsiders
questions.explanation: The subnet mask works with the IPv4 address to determine which subnet the device belongs to.

questions.question: What subnet mask is represented by the slash notation /20?
questions.explanation: /20 means 20 binary 1s in the mask, which is 255.255.240.0.

questions.question: A message is sent to all hosts on a remote network. Which type of message is it?
questions.explanation: A directed broadcast is sent to all hosts on a specific remote network.

questions.question: What are three characteristics of multicast transmission? (Choose three.)
options: The source address of a multicast transmission is in the range of 224.0.0.0 to 224.0.0.255.
A single packet can be sent to a group of hosts.
Multicast transmission can be used by routers to exchange routing information.
The range of 224.0.0.0 to 224.0.0.255 is reserved to reach multicast groups on a local network.
Computers use multicast transmission to request IPv4 addresses.
Multicast messages map lower layer addresses to upper layer addresses.
questions.explanation: Multicast sends one packet to a selected group of hosts, is used by routing protocols, and uses the 224.0.0.0 to 224.0.0.255 range for local multicast groups.

questions.question: Which three IP addresses are private? (Choose three.)
Which two IPv4 to IPv6 transition techniques manage the interconnection of IPv6 domains? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Dual stack lets devices run IPv4 and IPv6 together, and tunneling carries IPv6 packets across an IPv4 network.

questions.question: Which of these addresses is the shortest abbreviation for the IP address 3FFE:1044:0000:0000:00AB:0000:0000:0057?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros can be removed, and one continuous group of zero hextets can be compressed with ::. The valid shortest option is 3FFE:1044:0:0:AB::57.

questions.question: What type of address is automatically assigned to an interface when IPv6 is enabled on that interface?
questions.explanation: When IPv6 is enabled on an interface, it automatically generates a link-local address.

questions.question: What are two types of IPv6 unicast addresses? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Loopback and link-local are IPv6 unicast address types. IPv6 does not use broadcast.

questions.question: What are three parts of an IPv6 global unicast address? (Choose three.)
options: an interface ID that is used to identify the local network for a particular host
a global routing prefix that is used to identify the network portion of the address that has been provided by an ISP
a subnet ID that is used to identify networks inside of the local enterprise site
a global routing prefix that is used to identify the portion of the network address provided by a local administrator
an interface ID that is used to identify the local host on the network
questions.explanation: An IPv6 global unicast address includes a global routing prefix, a subnet ID, and an interface ID.

questions.question: An administrator wants to configure hosts to automatically assign IPv6 addresses to themselves by the use of Router Advertisement messages, but also to obtain the DNS server address from a DHCPv6 server. Which address assignment method should be configured?
questions.explanation: Stateless DHCPv6 uses Router Advertisement messages for address creation and DHCPv6 for extra information such as DNS server addresses.

questions.question: Which protocol supports Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (SLAAC) for dynamic assignment of IPv6 addresses to a host?
questions.explanation: SLAAC relies on ICMPv6 Router Advertisement messages.

questions.question: Which two things can be determined by using the ping command? (Choose two.)
options: the number of routers between the source and destination device
the IP address of the router nearest the destination device
the average time it takes a packet to reach the destination and for the response to return to the source
the destination device is reachable through the network
the average time it takes each router in the path between source and destination to respond
questions.explanation: Ping shows whether the destination is reachable and reports the round-trip response time.

questions.question: What is the purpose of ICMP messages?
options: to inform routers about network topology changes
to ensure the delivery of an IP packet
to provide feedback of IP packet transmissions
to monitor the process of a domain name to IP address resolution
questions.explanation: ICMP provides feedback about problems and status related to IP packet processing.

questions.question: What is indicated by a successful ping to the ::1 IPv6 address?
options: The default gateway address is correctly configured.
All hosts on the local link are available.
The link-local address is correctly configured.
IP is properly installed on the host.
questions.explanation: ::1 is the IPv6 loopback address. A successful ping to it confirms that the local IP stack is working.

questions.question: A user is executing a tracert to a remote device. At what point would a router, which is in the path to the destination device, stop forwarding the packet?
options: when the router receives an ICMP Time Exceeded message
when the RTT value reaches zero
when the host responds with an ICMP Echo Reply message
when the value in the TTL field reaches zero
when the values of both the Echo Request and Echo Reply messages reach zero
questions.explanation: Each router decrements TTL by 1. When TTL reaches zero, the router stops forwarding the packet and returns an ICMP Time Exceeded message.

questions.question: What is the binary equivalent of the decimal number 232?
questions.explanation: 232 equals 128 + 64 + 32 + 8, so the binary value is 11101000.

questions.question: What is the decimal equivalent of the binary number 10010101?
What field content is used by ICMPv6 to determine that a packet has expired?
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses the Hop Limit field to determine whether a packet has expired.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. The decimal equivalent of the binary number 10010101 is ____.
questions.explanation: Add the decimal values for the bit positions that contain 1: 128 + 16 + 4 + 1 = 149.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. The binary equivalent of the decimal number 232 is ____.
questions.explanation: 232 equals 128 + 64 + 32 + 8, so the binary value is 11101000.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. What is the decimal equivalent of the hex number 0x3F?
questions.explanation: Hex 3F equals 3 x 16 plus 15, which is 63.

questions.question: Match each description with an appropriate IP address. (Not all options are used.)
questions.explanation: 169.254.0.0/16 is link-local, 192.0.2.0/24 is TEST-NET, 240.0.0.0/4 is experimental, 172.16.0.0/12 is private, and 127.0.0.0/8 is loopback.

questions.question: If a network device has a mask of /28, how many IP addresses are available for hosts on this network?
questions.explanation: A /28 mask leaves 4 host bits. That gives 16 total addresses, but 2 are reserved for the network and broadcast addresses, leaving 14 usable host addresses.

questions.question: A network administrator is variably subnetting a network. The smallest subnet has a mask of 255.255.255.224. How many usable host addresses will this subnet provide?
questions.explanation: 255.255.255.224 is /27, leaving 5 host bits. 2^5 is 32 total addresses, and 30 are usable for hosts.

questions.question: Which statement is true about variable-length subnet masking?
options: Each subnet is the same size.
The size of each subnet may be different, depending on requirements.
Subnets may only be subnetted one additional time.
Bits are returned, rather than borrowed, to create additional subnets.
questions.explanation: VLSM allows different subnet sizes so each subnet can match the number of required hosts.

questions.question: Why does a Layer 3 device perform the ANDing process on a destination IP address and subnet mask?
options: to identify the broadcast address of the destination network
to identify the host address of the destination host
to identify the network address of the destination network
questions.explanation: ANDing an IP address with the subnet mask identifies the network address.

questions.question: How many usable IP addresses are available on the 192.168.1.0/27 network?
questions.explanation: A /27 mask leaves 5 host bits. 32 total addresses are possible, and 30 are usable host addresses.

questions.question: Which subnet mask would be used if exactly 4 host bits are available?
questions.explanation: Four host bits means 28 network bits, so the mask is /28 or 255.255.255.240.

questions.question: If a network device has a mask of /26, how many IP addresses are available for hosts on this network?
questions.explanation: A /26 mask leaves 6 host bits. 64 total addresses are possible, and 62 are usable for hosts.

questions.question: What is the prefix length notation for the subnet mask 255.255.255.224?
How many valid host addresses are available on an IPv4 subnet that is configured with a /26 mask?
questions.explanation: A /26 mask leaves 6 host bits. 64 addresses are possible, but 2 are reserved, leaving 62 valid host addresses.

questions.question: Which subnet mask would be used if 5 host bits are available?
questions.explanation: Five host bits means 27 network bits, so the mask is /27 or 255.255.255.224.

questions.question: A network administrator subnets the 192.168.10.0/24 network into subnets with /26 masks. How many equal-sized subnets are created?
questions.explanation: Moving from /24 to /26 borrows 2 bits for subnetting. 2^2 creates 4 equal-sized subnets.

questions.question: What are advantages of subnetting a large network? (Choose two.)
options: IP addresses can be reused on the same subnetwork.
Layer 3 devices are not required when a network is subnetted.
questions.explanation: Subnetting a large address space into smaller subnetworks helps to contain network traffic and thus improve network performance.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: What would allow devices on different subnets to be able to communicate?
questions.explanation: A router or Layer 3 switch is required for devices on different networks or subnets to be able to communicate.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: To create subnets, bits are borrowed from the ____ portion of an IP address.
questions.explanation: Subnets are created by borrowing bits from the host portion of an IP address to create additional network bits. The more bits borrowed, the more subnets created.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: How many subnets can be created if 4 bits are borrowed to specify subnets?
questions.explanation: Every bit borrowed can have one of two values, 0 or 1. The number of subnets created is 2^n, where n is the number of bits borrowed. With 4 borrowed bits, 16 subnets are created.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: What best describes a network broadcast address?
options: All 0 bits in the host portion of the address
All 0 bits plus a rightmost 1 bit in the host portion of the address
All 1 bits plus a rightmost 0 bit in the host portion of the address
All 1 bits in the host portion of the address
questions.explanation: A network broadcast address has all host bits turned on.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: How many valid host addresses are created when 4 host bits are borrowed from the 10.20.20.0/24 network?
questions.explanation: Borrowing 4 bits from a /24 leaves 4 host bits in each subnet. That creates 2^4 - 2, or 14, valid host addresses per subnet.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: A junior network technician has subnetted the 10.20.30.0/24 address space by borrowing 3 bits. The technician decides to use the second subnet for the Accounting department computers. Which of the following addresses could the network technician assign to hosts? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Borrowing 3 bits creates /27 subnets with 30 usable hosts. The second subnet is 10.20.30.32/27, with usable addresses 10.20.30.33 through 10.20.30.62.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: A junior network technician is assigning host addresses to devices in the 192.168.1.0/25 subnet. The departmental printer is assigned the address 192.168.1.131/25 with a 192.168.1.1/25 default gateway. No one in the department is able to print. What is the cause of the problem?
options: The default gateway is not correct for the departmental subnet.
The printer has been assigned a broadcast IP address.
The printer has been assigned an address on another subnet.
The printer has been assigned a network IP address.
questions.explanation: The 192.168.1.0/25 subnet ranges from 192.168.1.0 to 192.168.1.127. The printer address 192.168.1.131 is in another subnet.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: A new department has been established with 511 hosts that require addresses. Currently the company uses the 10.20.0.0/16 address space. How many bits must the network administrator borrow to provide addresses for this subnet without wasting addresses?
questions.explanation: The subnet must support at least 513 total addresses because network and broadcast addresses are unusable. The closest power of two is 1024, requiring 10 host bits. Starting with /16 leaves 16 host bits, so 6 bits can be borrowed.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: A network technician borrows 5 bits from the 10.0.0.0/16 network to create subnets. What is the subnet mask that should be associated with each of the newly created subnets?
questions.explanation: Borrowing 5 bits from a /16 network creates a /21 prefix. /21 is 255.255.248.0.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: ____ provides a more efficient IP address allocation by allowing the use of different-size subnets in the same network.
questions.explanation: With VLSM, different subnet masks can be used on different portions of the network, providing a more efficient allocation of available address space.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: A network administrator has borrowed 3 bits from the 10.20.0.0/25 network to create subnets. The administrator then decided to use the first subnet for point-to-point serial WAN connections each requiring two addresses. How many WAN connections can the administrator address using only the first subnet if he is using VLSM?
questions.explanation: Borrowing 3 bits from /25 creates /28 subnets with 4 host bits. For point-to-point links, VLSM can further subnet the first /28 into /30 networks. A /28 can be split into four /30 WAN subnets.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: A network administrator has decided to use VLSM to subnet the 10.11.0.0/20 network to provide addresses for two new departments and the point-to-point link that separates the two departments. The first department has 796 users and the second department has 31 users. The WAN link requires only two addresses. Which of the following subnets will provide the required contiguous space and waste the fewest addresses? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: 796 users require a /22, 31 users require a /26, and a point-to-point WAN link requires a /30. The matching contiguous subnets are 10.11.0.0/22, 10.11.253.0/26, and 10.11.253.64/30.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of subnetting IPv6 address space?
questions.explanation: Unlike IPv4, IPv6 address space is not scarce. IPv6 subnetting primarily supports hierarchical, logical network design.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: When subnetting IPv6 address space, why is it wise to subnet on a nibble boundary?
options: IPv6 is expressed in hexadecimal, and each nibble is one hexadecimal character.
You can only subnet IPv6 address space on nibble boundaries.
Subnetting on a nibble boundary is the most efficient use of IPv6 address space.
Subnetting on a nibble boundary is mandated by the Internet Numbering Authority.
questions.explanation: IPv6 is written in hexadecimal, and each nibble is one hexadecimal character. Subnetting on nibble boundaries makes subnet IDs easier to read and calculate.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: What is the third subnet address of the 2001:0DB8:ACAD::/48 network when borrowing 8 bits (2 nibbles)?
questions.explanation: Borrowing 8 bits from a /48 creates /56 subnets. Counting subnets from zero, the third subnet has 0002 in the subnet position: 2001:0DB8:ACAD:0002::/56.
questions.reference: User provided subnetting and IPv6 addressing questions

questions.question: What is a result of connecting two or more switches together?
options: The number of broadcast domains is increased.
The size of the broadcast domain is increased.
The number of collision domains is reduced.
The size of the collision domain is increased.
questions.explanation: Connecting switches together increases the size of the broadcast domain. Routers are needed to create separate broadcast domains.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. How many broadcast domains are there?
questions.explanation: A router separates broadcast domains. The exhibit shows four router interfaces connected to four switch segments, so there are four broadcast domains.
questions.imageAlt: Refer to the exhibit. How many broadcast domains are there?

questions.question: What are two reasons a network administrator might want to create subnets? (Choose two.)
options: reduction in number of routers needed
reduction in number of switches needed
questions.explanation: Subnets reduce overall traffic and improve performance. They also make it easier to apply security policies by subnet.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A company uses the address block of 128.107.0.0/16 for its network. What subnet mask would provide the maximum number of equal size subnets while providing enough host addresses for each subnet in the exhibit?
questions.explanation: The largest subnet needs 100 hosts. Seven host bits support 126 usable host addresses, so /25 or 255.255.255.128 gives enough hosts while maximizing equal-size subnets.
questions.imageAlt: Refer to the exhibit. A company uses the address block of 128.107.0.0/16 for its network. What subnet mask would provide the maximum number of equal size subnets while providing enough host addresses for each subnet in the exhibit?

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. The network administrator has assigned the LAN of LBMISS an address range of 192.168.10.0. This address range has been subnetted using a /29 prefix. The technician has decided to use the fifth subnet for configuring the new network. Which configuration should be entered into the properties of the workgroup server to allow connectivity to the Internet?
options: IP address: 192.168.10.65 subnet mask: 255.255.255.240, default gateway: 192.168.10.76
IP address: 192.168.10.38 subnet mask: 255.255.255.240, default gateway: 192.168.10.33
IP address: 192.168.10.38 subnet mask: 255.255.255.248, default gateway: 192.168.10.33
IP address: 192.168.10.41 subnet mask: 255.255.255.248, default gateway: 192.168.10.46
IP address: 192.168.10.254 subnet mask: 255.255.255.0, default gateway: 192.168.10.1
questions.explanation: With /29, subnets increment by 8. Counting subnet zero as the first subnet, the fifth subnet is 192.168.10.32/29. The first usable host is 192.168.10.33 and the last usable host is 192.168.10.38.
questions.imageAlt: Refer to the exhibit. The network administrator has assigned the LAN of LBMISS an address range of 192.168.10.0. This address range has been subnetted using a /29 prefix. The technician has decided to use the fifth subnet for configuring the new network. Which configuration should be entered into the properties of the workgroup server to allow connectivity to the Internet?

questions.question: How many host addresses are available on the network 172.16.128.0 with a subnet mask of 255.255.252.0?
questions.explanation: 255.255.252.0 is /22, leaving 10 host bits. That gives 2^10 - 2, or 1022, usable host addresses.

questions.question: How many bits must be borrowed from the host portion of an address to accommodate a router with five connected networks?
questions.explanation: Five connected networks need at least five subnets. Borrowing 3 bits creates 2^3, or 8, subnets.

questions.question: A network administrator wants to have the same network mask for all networks at a small site. The networks need 22, 20, 2, and 2 addresses. Which single subnet mask would make the most efficient use of 192.168.10.0/24 for the four subnetworks?
questions.explanation: The largest subnet needs 22 hosts. A /27 mask, 255.255.255.224, provides 30 usable host addresses and is the smallest equal mask that fits.

questions.question: A company has a network address of 192.168.1.64 with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.192. The company wants to create two subnetworks that would contain 10 hosts and 18 hosts respectively. Which two networks would achieve that? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: 192.168.1.64/27 supports 30 usable hosts and fits the 18-host subnet. 192.168.1.96/28 supports 14 usable hosts and fits the 10-host subnet.

questions.question: A network administrator is variably subnetting a network. The smallest subnet has a mask of 255.255.255.248. How many usable host addresses will this subnet provide?
questions.explanation: 255.255.255.248 is /29. It leaves 3 host bits, so 2^3 - 2 = 6 usable host addresses.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Given the network address of 192.168.5.0 and a subnet mask of 255.255.255.224, how many total host addresses are unused in the assigned subnets?
questions.explanation: Each /27 subnet has 30 usable addresses. Network A uses all 30, the two serial networks each use 2 and waste 28 each, and Network D uses 14 and wastes 16. Total unused addresses are 72.
questions.imageAlt: Refer to the exhibit. Given the network address of 192.168.5.0 and a subnet mask of 255.255.255.224, how many total host addresses are unused in the assigned subnets?

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Considering the addresses already used and remaining within the 10.16.10.0/24 network range, which subnet address could be assigned to the network containing 25 hosts?
questions.explanation: A subnet for 25 hosts needs /27. The available /27 range that fits without overlapping the used networks is 10.16.10.64/27.
questions.imageAlt: Refer to the exhibit. Considering the addresses already used and remaining within the 10.16.10.0/24 network range, which subnet address could be assigned to the network containing 25 hosts?

questions.question: A network administrator needs to monitor network traffic to and from servers in a data center. Which features of an IP addressing scheme should be applied to these devices?
options: random static addresses to improve security
addresses from different subnets for redundancy
predictable static IP addresses for easier identification
dynamic addresses to reduce the probability of duplicate addresses
questions.explanation: Predictable static IP addresses make servers easier to identify during monitoring and troubleshooting.

questions.question: Which two reasons generally make DHCP the preferred method of assigning IP addresses to hosts on large networks? (Choose two.)
options: It eliminates most address configuration errors.
It ensures that addresses are only applied to devices that require a permanent address.
It guarantees that every device that needs an address will get one.
It provides an address only to devices that are authorized to be connected to the network.
It reduces the burden on network support staff.
questions.explanation: DHCP reduces manual work for support staff and removes many address entry errors.

questions.question: A DHCP server is used to assign IP addresses dynamically to the hosts on a network. The address pool is configured with 192.168.10.0/24. There are 3 printers on this network that need reserved static IP addresses from the pool. How many IP addresses in the pool are left to be assigned to other hosts?
questions.explanation: A /24 network has 254 usable host addresses. Reserving 3 for printers leaves 251 addresses.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A company is deploying an IPv6 addressing scheme using site, sub-site, and subnet fields. What is the maximum number of subnets achieved per sub-site?
questions.explanation: The subnet field is one hexadecimal character. One hex character has 16 possible values, 0 through F.
questions.imageAlt: Refer to the exhibit. A company is deploying an IPv6 addressing scheme using site, sub-site, and subnet fields. What is the maximum number of subnets achieved per sub-site?

questions.question: What is the prefix for the host address 2001:DB8:BC15:A:12AB::1/64?
questions.explanation: A /64 prefix uses the first four hextets, so the prefix is 2001:DB8:BC15:A.

questions.question: Consider the range 2001:0DB8:BC15:00A0:0000:: through 2001:0DB8:BC15:00AF:0000::. What is the prefix length for the range of addresses?
questions.explanation: The common part is 2001:0DB8:BC15:00A. Each hexadecimal character represents 4 bits, so the prefix length is /60.

questions.question: Match the subnetwork to a host address that would be included within the subnetwork. (Not all options are used.)
Refer to the exhibit. Match the network with the correct IP address and prefix that will satisfy the usable host addressing requirements for each network. (Not all options are used.)
questions.explanation: Assign the largest subnet first: /25 for 100 hosts, /26 for 50 hosts, /27 for 25 hosts, and /30 for the point-to-point link.
questions.imageAlt: Refer to the exhibit. Match the network with the correct IP address and prefix that will satisfy the usable host addressing requirements for each network. (Not all options are used.)

questions.question: What two statements describe characteristics of Layer 3 broadcasts? (Choose two.)
options: Broadcasts are a threat and users must avoid using protocols that implement them.
There is a broadcast domain on each switch interface.
A limited broadcast packet has a destination IP address of 255.255.255.255.
A router will not forward any type of Layer 3 broadcast packet.
questions.explanation: Routers separate broadcast domains, and an IPv4 limited broadcast uses destination 255.255.255.255.

questions.question: Which network migration technique encapsulates IPv6 packets inside IPv4 packets to carry them over IPv4 network infrastructures?
questions.explanation: Tunneling carries IPv6 packets through an IPv4 infrastructure by encapsulating them inside IPv4 packets.

questions.question: Which two statements are correct about IPv4 and IPv6 addresses? (Choose two.)
options: IPv6 addresses are represented by hexadecimal numbers.
IPv4 addresses are represented by hexadecimal numbers.
IPv6 addresses are 32 bits in length.
IPv4 addresses are 32 bits in length.
IPv4 addresses are 128 bits in length.
IPv6 addresses are 64 bits in length.
questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are written in hexadecimal and are 128 bits long. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long.

questions.question: Which IPv6 address is most compressed for the full FE80:0:0:0:2AA:FF:FE9A:4CA3 address?
questions.explanation: The three consecutive zero hextets can be compressed once with ::, producing FE80::2AA:FF:FE9A:4CA3.

questions.question: An IPv6 enabled device sends a data packet with the destination address of FF02::1. What is the target of this packet?
options: all IPv6 enabled nodes on the local link
all IPv6 configured routers on the local link
all IPv6 configured routers across the network
questions.explanation: FF02::1 is the all-nodes multicast address on the local link.

questions.question: When a Cisco router is being moved from an IPv4 network to a complete IPv6 environment, which series of commands would correctly enable IPv6 forwarding and interface addressing?
options: configure terminal; interface fastethernet 0/0; ip address 192.168.1.254 255.255.255.0; no shutdown; ipv6 unicast-routing
configure terminal; interface fastethernet 0/0; ipv6 address 2001:db8:bced:1::9/64; no shutdown; exit; ipv6 unicast-routing
configure terminal; interface fastethernet 0/0; ipv6 address 2001:db8:bced:1::9/64; no shutdown
configure terminal; interface fastethernet 0/0; ip address 2001:db8:bced:1::9/64; ip address 192.168.1.254 255.255.255.0; no shutdown
questions.explanation: The interface needs an IPv6 address and no shutdown, and the router needs ipv6 unicast-routing enabled globally.

questions.question: Which two ICMP messages are used by both IPv4 and IPv6 protocols? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Route redirection and protocol unreachable exist in ICMP for both IPv4 and IPv6. Neighbor and router solicitation/advertisement are ICMPv6-specific functions.

questions.question: When an IPv6 enabled host needs to discover the MAC address of an intended IPv6 destination, which destination address is used by the source host in the NS message?
options: global unicast address of the receiver
questions.explanation: IPv6 Neighbor Solicitation uses the solicited-node multicast address for address resolution.

questions.question: What is a function of the tracert command that differs from the ping command when they are used on a workstation?
options: The tracert command reaches the destination faster.
The tracert command shows the information of routers in the path.
The tracert command sends one ICMP message to each hop in the path.
The tracert command is used to test the connectivity between two devices.
questions.explanation: The tracert command sends three pings to each hop (router) in the path toward the destination and displays the domain name and IP address of hops from their responses. Because tracert uses the ping command, the travel time is the same as a standalone ping command. The primary function of a standalone ping command is to test the connectivity between two hosts.

questions.question: Which ICMP message is used by the traceroute utility during the process of finding the path between two end hosts?
questions.explanation: Traceroute progressively increments the TTL (IPv4) or hop limit (IPv6) field for sending a sequence of ping commands. When a router senses that the TTL or hop limit is 0, it discards the packet and sends a time exceeded message to the source. The returned message contains the IP address of the router that discarded the packet.

questions.question: Which two things can be determined by using the ping command? (Choose two.)
options: the number of routers between the source and destination device
the IP address of the router nearest the destination device
the average time it takes a packet to reach the destination and for the response to return to the source
the destination device is reachable through the network
the average time it takes each router in the path between source and destination to respond
questions.explanation: A ping command provides feedback on the time between when an echo request was sent to a remote host and when the echo reply was received. A successful ping also indicates that the destination host was reachable through the network.

questions.question: Which statement describes a characteristic of the traceroute utility?
options: It sends four Echo Request messages.
It utilizes the ICMP Source Quench messages.
It is primarily used to test connectivity between two hosts.
It identifies the routers in the path from a source host to a destination host.
questions.explanation: Traceroute is a utility that generates a list of hops (or routers) along the path from a source host to the destination host.

questions.question: Which utility uses the Internet Control Messaging Protocol (ICMP)?
questions.explanation: ICMP is used by network devices to send error messages, and the ping utility uses ICMP echo request and echo reply messages.

questions.question: A network administrator can successfully ping the server at www.cisco.com, but cannot ping the company web server located at an ISP in another city. Which tool or command would help identify the specific router where the packet was lost or delayed?
questions.explanation: The traceroute command provides connectivity information about the path a packet takes to reach the destination and about every router (hop) along the way. It also indicates how long a packet takes to get from the source to each hop and back.

questions.question: Which protocol is used by IPv4 and IPv6 to provide error messaging?
questions.explanation: ICMP is used by IPv4 and IPv6 to provide for messages to be sent in the event of certain errors and for informational purposes.

questions.question: What message is sent by a host to check the uniqueness of an IPv6 address before using that address?
questions.explanation: In IPv6, Duplicate Address Detection (DAD) is used in place of ARP. An IPv6 host performs DAD by sending a neighbor solicitation (NS) message to its own IPv6 address to ensure the uniqueness of the address prior to using it.

questions.question: A technician is troubleshooting a network where it is suspected that a defective node in the network path is causing packets to be dropped. The technician only has the IP address of the end point device and does not have any details of the intermediate devices. What command can the technician use to identify the faulty node?
questions.explanation: The tracert command identifies each hop in the path to a destination, which can help locate the node where packets are dropped.

questions.question: A user who is unable to connect to the file server contacts the help desk. The helpdesk technician asks the user to ping the IP address of the default gateway that is configured on the workstation. What is the purpose for this ping command?
options: to obtain a dynamic IP address from the server
to request that gateway forward the connection request to the file server
to test that the host has the capability to reach hosts on other networks
to resolve the domain name of the file server to its IP address
questions.explanation: The ping command is used to test connectivity between hosts. Pinging the default gateway tests whether the host has the capability to reach hosts on its own network and on other networks.

questions.question: A user calls to report that a PC cannot access the internet. The network technician asks the user to issue the command ping 127.0.0.1 in a command prompt window. The user reports that the result is four positive replies. What conclusion can be drawn based on this connectivity test?
options: The PC can access the network. The problem exists beyond the local network.
The IP address obtained from the DHCP server is correct.
The PC can access the Internet. However, the web browser may not work.
questions.explanation: The ping 127.0.0.1 command verifies that the TCP/IP stack is functional. This loopback test does not send traffic beyond the PC itself.

questions.question: Which command can be used to test connectivity between two devices using echo request and echo reply messages?
questions.explanation: Ping is used to test connectivity between end devices. It uses ICMP echo request and echo reply messages.

questions.question: What field content is used by ICMPv6 to determine that a packet has expired?
questions.explanation: ICMPv6 sends a Time Exceeded message if the router cannot forward an IPv6 packet because the packet expired. The router uses the Hop Limit field to determine if the packet has expired.

questions.question: Which protocol provides feedback from the destination host to the source host about errors in packet delivery?
questions.explanation: The ICMP protocol operates at Layer 3 of the OSI model, which is the Internet layer of the TCP/IP model. ICMP encapsulates the ping and traceroute commands.

questions.question: A network administrator is testing network connectivity by issuing the ping command on a router. Which symbol will be displayed to indicate that a time expired during the wait for an ICMP echo reply message?
questions.explanation: When the ping command is issued on a router, ! indicates receipt of an ICMP echo reply message, . indicates a timeout while waiting for an ICMP echo reply message, and U indicates that an ICMP unreachable message was received.

questions.question: Which feature on a Cisco router permits the forwarding of traffic for which there is no specific route?
questions.explanation: A default static route is used as a gateway of last resort to forward unknown destination traffic to a next hop/exit interface. The next-hop or exit interface is the destination to send traffic to on a network after the traffic is matched in a router. The route source is the location a route was learned from.

questions.question: Which three advantages are provided by static routing? (Choose three.)
options: Static routing does no advertise over the network, thus providing better security.
No intervention is required to maintain changing route information.
Static routes scale well as the network grows.
The path a static route uses to send data is known.
Configuration of static routes is error-free.
Static routing typically uses less network bandwidth and fewer CPU operations than dynamic routing does.
questions.explanation: Static routes are prone to errors from incorrect configuration by the administrator. They do not scale well, because the routes must be manually reconfigured to accommodate a growing network. Intervention is required each time a route change is necessary. They do provide better security, use less bandwidth, and provide a known path to the destination.

questions.question: What are two functions of dynamic routing protocols? (Choose two.)
options: to choose the path that is specified by the administrator
questions.explanation: Dynamic routing protocols exist to discover the network, maintain routing tables, and calculate the best path. Having low levels of routing overhead, using the path specified by the administrator, and avoiding the exposure of network information are functions of static routing.

questions.question: What is an advantage of using dynamic routing protocols instead of static routing?
options: more secure in controlling routing updates
ability to actively search for new routes if the current path becomes unavailable
questions.explanation: Dynamic routing has the ability to search and find a new best path if the current path is no longer available. The other options are actually the advantages of static routing.

questions.question: Which value represents the "trustworthiness" of a route and is used to determine which route to install into the routing table when there are multiple routes toward the same destination?
questions.explanation: The administrative distance represents the trustworthiness of a particular route. The lower an administrative distance, the more trustworthy the learned route is. When a router learns multiple routes toward the same destination, the router uses the administrative distance value to determine which route to place into the routing table. A metric is used by a routing protocol to compare routes received from the routing protocol. An exit interface is the interface used to send a packet in the direction of the destination network. A routing protocol is used to exchange routing updates between two or more adjacent routers.

questions.question: Which packet-forwarding method does a router use to make switching decisions when it is using a forwarding information base and an adjacency table?
questions.explanation: Cisco Express Forwarding (CEF) is the fastest and preferred switching method. It uses a FIB and an adjacency table to perform the task of packet switching. These data structures change with the topology.

questions.question: Which type of route would typically be used on a border router so that devices inside the company could access the Internet?
questions.explanation: A default route is commonly used on the edge router of a company to connect to an ISP. A default route is a specialized static route that uses the network number and mask of all 0s (0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0). For this reason, it is sometimes known as a quad zero route.

questions.question: What are two functions of a router? (Choose two.)
options: A router connects multiple IP networks.
It determines the best path to send packets.
It builds a routing table based on ARP requests.
It controls the flow of data via the use of Layer 2 addresses.
questions.explanation: Routers connect multiple networks, determine the best path to send packets, and forward packets based on a destination IP address.

questions.question: When a router learns that multiple paths are available to a destination network from the same routing protocol, which factor is considered by a router to choose the best path to forward a packet?
options: the reliability value of the neighboring routers
the fastest bandwidth of exiting interfaces
the order of paths on the routing table
questions.explanation: When a router learns that multiple paths are available to a destination network from the same routing protocol, the route with the lowest metric is put into the routing table to forward packets toward that network.

questions.question: Which two route source codes are automatically created within a routing table whenever a router interface is configured with an IP address and activated? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Directly connected and local routes are automatically created whenever an interface is configured with an IP address and activated.

questions.question:
The output of the show ip route command contains the following entry:
S 10.2.0.0 [1/0] via 172.16.2.2.
What value is indicated by the 1 in the [1/0] portion of the output?
options: interface ID through which the network can be reached
questions.explanation: In the routing table entry, S 10.2.0.0 [1/0] via 172.16.2.2, the numbers inside the bracket indicate the administrative distance and metric respectively.

questions.question: Which type of static route creates a gateway of last resort?
questions.explanation: There are four basic types of static routes. Floating static routes are backup routes that are placed into the routing table if a primary route is lost. A summary static route aggregates several routes into one, reducing the size of the routing table. Standard static routes are entered manually into the routing table. Default static routes create a gateway of last resort.

questions.question: What are two common types of static routes in routing tables? (Choose two)
options: a static route converted from a route that is learned through a dynamic routing protocol
a static route to a specific network
a static route shared between two neighboring routers
a built-in static route by IOS
questions.explanation: There are two common types of static routes in a routing table, namely, a static route to a specific network and a default static route. A static route configured on a router can be distributed by the router to other neighboring routers. However, the distributed static route will be a little different in the routing table on neighboring routers.

questions.question: What are two reasons why an administrator might choose to use static routing rather than dynamic routing? (Choose two.)
options: Static routing uses less router processing and bandwidth.
Static routing is easier to maintain in large networks.
Static routing does not require complete knowledge of the whole network.
questions.explanation: Because static routes must be created and changed manually, they require a larger investment of administrative time and do not scale easily. Static routes do not require additional CPU cycles to calculate and advertise routes, and they provide more security because they are not advertised over the network. Proper implementation of static routes requires the administrator to have a complete understanding of the network topology.

questions.question: What address and prefix length is used when configuring an IPv6 default static route?
questions.explanation: The IPv6 address and prefix for a default static route is ::/0. This represents all zeros in the address and a prefix length of zero.

questions.question: What are two advantages of static routing over dynamic routing? (Choose two.)
options: Static routing is more secure because it does not advertise routes to other routers.
Static routing is relatively easy to configure for large networks.
Static routing requires very little knowledge of the network for correct implementation.
Static routing scales well with expanding networks.
Static routing uses fewer router resources than dynamic routing.
questions.explanation: Static routing requires a thorough understanding of the entire network for proper implementation. It can be prone to errors and does not scale well for large networks. Static routing uses fewer router resources because no computing is required for updating routes. Static routing can also be more secure because it does not advertise over the network.

questions.question: What type of route allows a router to forward packets even though its routing table contains no specific route to the destination network?
questions.explanation: A static default route is a catch-all route for all unmatched networks.

questions.question: The network administrator configures the router with the ip route 172.16.1.0 255.255.255.0 172.16.2.2 command. How will this route appear in the routing table?
questions.explanation: The route will appear in the routing with a code of S (Static).

questions.question: R1 is configured with the ip route 10.1.0.0 255.255.0.0 g0/0/0 command. What happens if the G0/0/0 interface goes down?
options: The manually configured route remains in the routing table.
The router polls neighbors for a replacement route.
The router redirects the static route to a backup interface.
The static route is removed from the routing table.
questions.explanation: When the interface associated with a static route goes down, the router will remove the route because it is no longer valid.

questions.question: What static route identifies the gateway IP address to which the router sends all IP packets for which it does not have a learned route?
questions.explanation: A default static route is a route that matches all packets. It identifies the gateway IP address to which the router sends all IP packets for which it does not have a learned or static route. A default static route is simply a static route with 0.0.0.0/0 as the destination IPv4 address or ::/0 for IPv6. Configuring a default static route creates a gateway of last resort.

questions.question: On which type of network would a dynamic routing protocol be implemented in?
options: On a home network router with wireless clients.
On a network that commonly experiences topology changes.
On a small two router network.
On a stub network connecting to a provider.
questions.explanation: Dynamic routing protocols consume more router resources, are suitable for larger networks, and are more useful on networks that are growing and changing.

questions.question: Which value in a routing table is used to compare routes received from a routing protocol?
questions.explanation: A metric is used by a routing protocol to compare routes received from the routing protocol. An exit interface is the interface used to send a packet in the direction of the destination network. A routing protocol is used to exchange routing updates between two or more adjacent routers. The administrative distance represents the trustworthiness of a particular route. The lower an administrative distance, the more trustworthy the learned route is. When a router learns multiple routes toward the same destination, the router uses the administrative distance value to determine which route to place into the routing table.

questions.question: A network administrator configures the G0/0/0 interface with the ip address 10.1.1.0 255.255.255.0 command. However, when the administrator issues the show ip route command, the routing table does not show the directly connected network. What is the possible cause of the problem?
options: No packets with a destination network of 172.16.1.0 have been sent to R1.
The configuration needs to be saved first.
The G0/0/0 interface has not been activated.
The subnet mask is incorrect for the IPv4 address.
questions.explanation: A directly connected network will be added to the routing table when these three conditions are met: (1) the interface is configured with a valid IP address; (2) it is activated with the no shutdown command; and (3) it receives a carrier signal from another device that is connected to the interface. An incorrect subnet mask for an IPv4 address will not prevent its appearance in the routing table, although the error may prevent successful communications.

questions.question: A network administrator configures a router by the command ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 209.165.200.226. What is the purpose of this command?
options: to forward all packets to the device with IP address 209.165.200.226
to forward packets destined for the network 0.0.0.0 to the device with IP address 209.165.200.226
to provide a route to forward packets for which there is no route in the routing table
to add a dynamic route for the destination network 0.0.0.0 to the routing table
questions.explanation: The command ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <next hop> adds a default route to the routing table of a router. When the router receives a packet and does not have a specific route toward the destination, it forwards the packet to the next hop indicated in the default route. A route created with the ip route command is a static route, not a dynamic route.

questions.question: Which type of static route that is configured on a router uses only the exit interface?
questions.explanation: When only the exit interface is used, the route is a directly connected static route. When the next-hop IP address is used, the route is a recursive static route. When both are used, it is a fully specified static route.

questions.question: A network administrator uses the command ip route 172.18.0.0 255.255.0.0 S0/0/1 to configure a floating static route on a router. That route will function as a backup route to reach the EIGRP learned network 172.18.0.0/16. After this configuration, the EIGRP route is removed from the routing table even though EIGRP is still functioning properly. Why is the static route not functioning as intended?
options: The network mask is incorrectly configured.
The next hop neighbor IP address is not configured.
The destination network is incorrectly configured.
The administrative distance value is not high enough on the static route.
questions.explanation: A floating static route requires an administrative distance greater than that of the dynamic routing protocol in order to be used as a backup route. In this problem an administrative distance greater than 90 would have to be added to the static route: ip route 172.18.0.0 255.255.0.0 S0/0/1 100.

questions.question: What type of static route is created when the next-hop IP address and exit interface are specified?
questions.explanation: A fully specified static route has the next-hop IP address and exit interface specified. A recursive static route has only the next-hop IP address specified. A directly attached static route has only the router exit interface specified. A floating static route has a higher metric than the dynamic routes and serves as a backup route.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax of a floating static route?
questions.explanation: Floating static routes are used as backup routes, often to routes learned from dynamic routing protocols. To be a floating static route, the configured route must have a higher administrative distance than the primary route. For example, if the primary route is learned through OSPF, then a floating static route that serves as a backup to the OSPF route must have an administrative distance greater than 110. The administrative distance on a floating static route is put at the end of the static route: ip route 209.165.200.228 255.255.255.248 10.0.0.1 120.

questions.question: Which static route statement shows a recursive IPv6 static route?
questions.explanation: In a recursive static route, only the next-hop IPv6 address is specified. As a consequence, the router must perform a recursive route table lookup to find an exit interface associated with the network of the IPv6 address.

questions.question: A network administrator is configuring a route to forward packets to a specific web server. What type of route should be configured by the administrator?
options: a static route with an administrative distance higher than 1
questions.explanation: A host route is a route installed in the routing table where the destination address has a subnet mask of /32 for IPv4 or /128 for IPv6, an address of a specific device. A host route can allow for a more efficient processing of packets that are directed to the device, rather than for packet forwarding, such as by a default route, an OSPF route, or an EIGRP route.

questions.question: Which command would create a valid IPv6 default route?
questions.explanation: The correct prefix and prefix length for a default route is ::/0, which matches any address. ::/128 matches only the specific address of all zeros. When creating a static route that uses a link-local address as the next hop, an exit interface must also be specified for the route to be valid.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of a default static route? ​
options: It backs up a route already discovered by a dynamic routing protocol.
It is configured with a higher administrative distance than is the original dynamic routing protocol.
It uses a single network address to send multiple static routes to one destination address.
It identifies the gateway IP address to which the router sends all IP packets for which it does not have a learned or static route.
questions.explanation: A default static route is a route that matches all packets. It identifies the gateway IP address to which the router sends all IP packets for which the router does not have a learned or static route. A default static route is simply a static route with 0.0.0.0/0 as the destination IPv4 address. Configuring a default static route creates a gateway of last resort.​

questions.question: What is the purpose of a floating static route?
options: It is commonly used when a dynamic routing protocol is not being used.
It allows connectivity to remote destinations that are not contained in the routing table.
It allows summarization of contiguous networks.
It allows an alternate connection to be used when the preferred link fails.
questions.explanation: A floating static route is a backup route with an administrative distance that is higher than a dynamically learned route or another static route. The purpose of a floating static route is to use a particular path to a destination network that is not the best route, but is used only when the preferred route is down.

questions.question: Which IPv6 static route would serve as a backup route to a dynamic route learned through OSPF?
questions.explanation: The command ipv6 route 2001:db8:acad:1::/32 2001:db8:acad:6::2 200, specifies a floating static route to the 2001:db8:acad:1::/32 network with an administrative distance of 200. Since OSPF has an administrative distance of 110, the static route would only be placed in the routing table if the OSPF learned route was removed.

questions.question:
What command, or set of commands, would be used to determine if the following configuration on router HQ works as designed?
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 serial 0/0/0 10 
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 serial 0/1/0
options:
HQ(config)# interface serial 0/1/0
HQ(config-if)# shutdown
HQ(config-if)# end
HQ# show ip route
questions.explanation: To test a floating static route, take down the main route/link in order to see whether the backup link appears in the routing table. The show ip route command simply shows the routing table. Only one of the static routes would be shown at any one time.

questions.question: Which type of static route typically uses the distance parameter in the ip route global configuration command?
questions.explanation: Because a floating static route is not designed to be used as a primary route, its configuration requires a higher administrative distance than the usual default value of 1. When set higher than the administrative distance for the current routing protocol, the distance parameter allows the route to be used only when the primary route fails. All other forms of static routes have specific uses as primary routes.

questions.question: Why would a floating static route be configured with an administrative distance that is higher than the administrative distance of a dynamic routing protocol that is running on the same router?
options: to be used as a backup route
to act as a gateway of last resort
to be the priority route in the routing table
questions.explanation: By default, dynamic routing protocols have a higher administrative distance than static routes. Configuring a static route with a higher administrative distance than that of the dynamic routing protocol will result in the dynamic route being used instead of the static route. However, should the dynamically learned route fail, then the static route will be used as a backup.

questions.question: What network address and subnet mask combination would be used to create a default static route that matches any IPv4 destination?
questions.explanation: For a route to be considered a default static route it must use a network ID and subnetmask combination that will match any destination IP address. The address and mask of 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 in a static route will create a route table entry that matches any destination.

questions.question: Assume the administrator has entered the ip route 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 10.10.10.2 5 command. How would an administrator test this configuration?
options: Delete the default gateway route on the router.
Manually shut down the router interface used as a primary route.
Ping any valid address on the 192.168.10.0/24 network.
Ping from the 192.168.10.0 network to the 10.10.10.2 address.
questions.explanation: A floating static route is a backup route that only appears in the routing table when the interface used with the primary route is down. To test a floating static route, the route must be in the routing table. Therefore, shutting down the interface used as a primary route would allow the floating static route to appear in the routing table.

questions.question: What route has the highest administrative distance?
options: A route received through the EIGRP routing protocol
A route received through the OSPF routing protocol
questions.explanation: The most believable route or the route with the lowest administrative distance is one that is directly connected to a router. In order of trustworthiness is A (AD = 0), D (Static route AD = 1), B (EIGRP AD = 90), and C (OSPF AD = 110). Therefore, the OSPF routes are considered to be the least trustworthy.

questions.question: Which route would be used to forward a packet with a source IP address of 10.10.10.1 and a destination IP address of 172.16.1.1?
questions.explanation: Even though OSPF has a higher administrative distance value (less trustworthy), the best match is the route in the routing table that has the greatest number of far-left matching bits.

questions.question: Which static route is a fully specified static route?
questions.explanation: A fully specified static route can be used to avoid recursive routing table lookups by the router. A fully specified static route contains both the IP address of the next-hop router and the ID of the exit interface.

questions.question: Which type of route could be configured to be a backup route for a dynamic routing protocol?
questions.explanation: By default, dynamic routing protocols have a higher administrative distance than static routes. Configuring a static route with a higher administrative distance than that of the dynamic routing protocol will result in the dynamic route being used instead of the static route. However, should the dynamically learned route fail, the static route will be used as a backup.

questions.question: On which router would a default static route be configured?
options: A router providing DHCP services to clients.
A router that is connected to multiple providers.
A stub router connecting to a service provider.
On all routers in the network.
questions.explanation: A stub router or an edge router connected to an ISP has only one other router as a connection. A default static route works in those situations because all traffic will be sent to one destination. The destination router is the gateway of last resort. The default route is not configured on the gateway, but on the router sending traffic to the gateway.

questions.question: What network prefix and prefix-length combination is used to create a default static route that will match any IPv6 destination?
questions.explanation: A default static route configured for IPv6 is a network prefix of all zeros and a prefix mask of 0, which is expressed as ::/0.

questions.question: How would you test a floating static route?
options: Delete the default gateway route on the router.
Manually shut down the router interface used as a primary route.
Ping any valid address on the 192.168.10.0/24 network.
Ping from the 192.168.10.0 network to the 10.10.10.2 address.
questions.explanation: A floating static route is a backup route that only appears in the routing table when the interface used with the primary route is down. To test a floating static route, the route must be in the routing table. Therefore, shutting down the interface used as a primary route would allow the floating static route to appear in the routing table.

questions.question: Which three advantages are provided by static routing? (Choose three.)

Intervention is required each time a route change is necessary. They do provide better security, use less bandwidth, and provide a known path to the destination.
options: Static routing does not advertise over the network, thus providing better security.
Configuration of static routes is error-free.
Static routes scale well as the network grows.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. This network has two connections to the ISP, one via router C and one via router B. questions.explanation:
Explanation: Topic 14.4.9
After a router determines the destination network by ANDing the destination IP address with the subnet mask, the router examines the routing table for the resulting destination network number. When a match is found, the packet is sent to the interface associated with the network number. When no routing table entry is found for the particular network, the default gateway or gateway of last resort (if configured or known) is used. If there is no gateway of last resort, the packet is dropped. In this instance, the 192.168.12.224 network is not found in the routing table and the router uses the gateway of last resort. The gateway of last resort is the IP address of 209.165.200.226. The router knows this is an IP address that is associated with the 209.165.200.224 network. The router then proceeds to transmit the packet out the Serial0/0/0 interface, or the interface that is associated with 209.165.200.224.

Which route would have to go down in order for this static route to appear in the routing table?
questions.reference: CCNA 2 v7 Modules 14-16 Routing Concepts and Configuration Exam
questions.explanation:
Explanation: Topic 15.4.1
The administrative distance of 5 added to the end of the static route creates a floating static situation for a static route that goes down. Static routes have a default administrative distance of 1. This route that has an administrative distance of 5 will not be placed into the routing table unless the previously entered static route to the 192.168.10.0/24 goes down or was never entered. The administrative distance of 5 added to the end of the static route configuration creates a floating static route that will be placed in the routing table when the primary route to the same destination network goes down. By default, a static route to the 192.168.10.0/24 network has an administrative distance of 1. Therefore, the floating route with an administrative distance of 5 will not be placed into the routing table unless the previously entered static route to the 192.168.10.0/24 goes down or was never entered. Because the floating route has an administrative distance of 5, the route is preferred to an OSPF-learned route (with the administrative distance of 110) or an EIGRP-learned route (with the administrative distance of 110) to the same destination network.

an OSPF-learned route to the 192.168.10.0/24 network
an EIGRP-learned route to the 192.168.10.0/24 network
